title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER CALLS FOR A COMMON DIGITAL AUDIT MONITORING PLATFORM FOR STATE LEGISLATURES ON THE LINES OF PARLIAMENT
subtitle:
CENTRE AND STATES MUST WORK IN TANDEM TO EVOLVE A ROBUST SYSTEM OF AUDIT AND EVALUATION FOR MORE EFFECTIVE LEGISLATIVE OVERSIGHT: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

KERALAM RESOLUTION TO PROVIDE A DEFINING ROADMAP FOR STRENGTHENING PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEES AND DEEPENING LEGISLATIVE OVERSIGHT: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

CAPACITY BUILDING AND TRAINING IN EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES IS NECESSARY FOR PAC MEMBERS, CAG OFFICIALS, AND LEGISLATIVE STAFF: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

BEST PRACTICES AND TECHNOLOGICAL INNOVATIONS OF STATE PACs MUST BE SHARED AND REPLICATED ACROSS THE COUNTRY: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER ADDRESSES VALEDICTORY SESSION OF THE CONFERENCE OF CHAIRPERSONS OF PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEES OF PARLIAMENT AND STATE/UT LEGISLATURES AT THIRUVANANTHAPURAM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 4:08PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Delivering the valedictory address on the conclusion of the two-day Conference of Chairpersons of Public Accounts Committees of the Parliament of India and States/UTs Legislatures at Thiruvananthapuram today, Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla called for greater technological integration in the functioning of legislative committees. Proposing a common digital Audit Monitoring Platform for state legislatures on the lines of the platform available to the committees of Parliament, he said that such a platform would facilitate systematic monitoring of audit observations, strengthen follow-up mechanisms, and ensure the timely examination and disposal of audit reports.
Emphasising that technology must become an instrument of institutional transformation, he noted that the adoption of digital innovations would significantly enhance the efficiency, transparency, and effectiveness of legislative oversight. At the same time, cautioning against overdependence on technology, he observed that technological advancement must always remain anchored in human values, wisdom, and sensitivity. Technology should reinforce institutional accountability and improve the quality of decision-making, but it can never substitute human judgment and discernment. He also underscored the need to maintain the accuracy, authenticity, and impartiality of data generated and accessed through digital platforms, observing that the credibility of technology-driven governance ultimately rests on the reliability of the information on which decisions are based.
Referring to the suggestions made during the conference by the Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee of Lok Sabha Shri K. C. Venugopal, Lok Sabha Speaker called for the committees of Parliament and state legislatures to jointly evolve a comprehensive system of audit and evaluation to address common challenges relating to continuous scrutiny and timely disposal of audit reports. He observed that a coordinated institutional mechanism would foster greater synergy, facilitate the exchange of experiences, and strengthen the collective capacity of Public Accounts Committees across the country.
Underscoring the indispensable role of PACs in ensuring accountability in public expenditure, he said that while the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) conducts independent and impartial audits, the Public Accounts Committees shoulder the crucial responsibility of examining audit findings, undertaking detailed factual scrutiny, and ensuring effective follow-up on their recommendations. He stressed that audit observations must not remain confined to reports and records; they must translate into appropriate corrective measures and tangible improvements in administrative functioning. The Executive, he said, must accord due importance to the recommendations of these committees and ensure their timely implementation.
Noting that the Keralam Resolution adopted at the Conference of Chairpersons of Public Accounts Committees (PACs) of Parliament and State/UT Legislatures will serve as a significant guiding framework and a forward-looking roadmap for strengthening the functioning of these vital parliamentary and legislative institutions in the years ahead, he observed that the rich deliberations, collective wisdom, and recommendations emerging from the conference must find meaningful expression in concrete action. He emphasised that the ultimate objective must be to strengthen financial discipline, enhance institutional capabilities, and make governance more transparent, responsive, and outcome-oriented at both the Union and state levels. Expressing confidence that its recommendations would find meaningful reflection in the functioning of both the legislature and the executive, he stated that the effective implementation of the resolution would further strengthen democratic institutions, reinforce public trust, and enhance the quality of parliamentary and legislative oversight.
Lok Sabha Speaker mentioned that the expanding scale of public investment in vital sectors such as education, healthcare, infrastructure, social welfare, and rural development has made the responsibility of ensuring the prudent and purposeful utilisation of public funds even more significant. Every rupee of public money, he emphasised, must be properly accounted for and utilised for the purpose for which it was allocated.
He observed that legislative oversight must, therefore, go beyond the examination of expenditure to assess whether public funds are delivering the intended benefits and creating measurable improvements in the lives of citizens. He  further emphasised that the evaluation of government programmes and schemes must encompass their continuity, quality, timely implementation, and actual outcomes. Whether it is the creation of durable infrastructure, the completion of projects within stipulated timelines, or the timely delivery of welfare benefits to eligible beneficiaries, every aspect of public service delivery must be subjected to systematic scrutiny and evaluation. He observed that while department-related standing committees also undertake important assessments in this regard, the Public Accounts Committee has a particularly significant responsibility in ensuring financial propriety and accountability for public expenditure.
Highlighting the importance of strengthening institutional capabilities, Shri Birla said that continuous capacity building and professional development of officers and employees associated with the CAG and Public Accounts Committees are essential in an era of rapid technological transformation. Members of Parliament and state legislatures must also be equipped with the requisite knowledge and skills to understand and effectively employ emerging technologies in their oversight responsibilities. Regular training, exposure to new tools, and the sharing of professional expertise, he noted, would considerably enhance the quality of scrutiny, monitoring, and evaluation.
Lok Sabha Speaker also called for institutionalising regular meetings, conferences, and exchanges of experiences among Public Accounts Committees of Parliament and state legislatures. He observed that the sharing of successful practices, innovative approaches, and technological solutions developed by different states would provide valuable learning opportunities and enable committees across the country to adopt and replicate effective models. Noting that representatives from 27 states participated in the conference and enriched the deliberations with their experiences and perspectives, he said that such collective engagement is essential to building stronger and more effective legislative institutions.
Shri Birla noted that the true significance of the conference would lie in translating its deliberations and the Kerala Resolution into sustained institutional action. He emphasised that stronger Public Accounts Committees, backed by modern technology, informed scrutiny, and effective follow-up mechanisms, would contribute significantly to ensuring that public resources are utilised with prudence, integrity, and a clear sense of public purpose.
PACs MUST EVOLVE WITH CHANGING TIMES TO ENSURE EFFECTIVE ACCOUNTABILITY OF PUBLIC MONEY: SHRI K. C. VENUGOPAL
Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament emphasised that PACs must evolve with changing times to ensure accountability as public money moves through increasingly complex channels. Observing that PACs translate audit findings presented to legislatures into meaningful accountability, he stressed the need for timely audits of public schemes and the prompt laying of audit reports before the Houses. He expressed concern over delayed, incomplete, or absent replies from ministries and departments, and called upon the executive to furnish complete responses promptly.
Emphasising that the work of PACs must reach the people, he suggested that at least one PAC report be taken up for discussion in Parliament and each state legislature to strengthen accountability. He also called for better coordination between the Centre and states in scrutinising Centrally Sponsored Schemes and proposed at least one annual meeting between Union and state PACs devoted to these schemes. Underlining the importance of specialised staff, training, and capacity building, he advocated greater use of technology, including a dashboard to track audit paragraphs and action taken.
Speaker of the Kerala Legislative Assembly;  Deputy Speaker of the Kerala Legislative Assembly and the Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee of Kerala also remained present on this occasion.
The two-day conference witnessed extensive and constructive deliberations on the theme “Audit, Accountability, and Good Governance – The Evolving Role of the PAC”, with a particular focus on strengthening financial oversight, improving audit follow-up mechanisms, embracing technological innovations, and enhancing the institutional effectiveness of Public Accounts Committees.
केरलम विधान सभा, तिरुवनंतपुरम में आयोजित दो दिवसीय Conference of Chairpersons of Public Accounts Committees of Parliament of India and State/UT Legislatures के समापन समारोह को संबोधित किया।

केरलम की धरती पर, जहां एक समृद्ध लोकतांत्रिक परंपरा रही है, देश के 27 प्रदेशों से पधारे PAC प्रतिनिधियों ने दो दिनों तक इस विषय पर व्यापक विचार-विमर्श किया कि देश और राज्यों की लोक लेखा समितियां किस प्रकार सार्वजनिक वित्त प्रबंधन में वित्तीय अनुशासन, पारदर्शिता और जवाबदेही सुनिश्चित करते हुए कार्य करें।

इस सम्मेलन में सभी के सहयोग और सहभागिता से निम्न साझा संकल्प प्रस्ताव भी पारित हुआ -

- सार्वजनिक धन के आवंटन एवं उपयोग की कड़ी जांच कर निर्धारित उद्देश्यों के लिए उसका उचित उपयोग सुनिश्चित करना;
- संसद एवं राज्य/केंद्रशासित प्रदेशों की लोक लेखा समितियों के बीच संवाद, अनुभवों और Best Practices के आदान-प्रदान हेतु डिजिटल पोर्टल विकसित करना;
- ऑडिट पैरा एवं PAC की सिफारिशों पर Action Taken Reports प्रस्तुत करने की समय-सीमा निर्धारित करना;
- सभी राज्यों/केंद्रशासित प्रदेशों में Audit Para Monitoring System जैसी डिजिटल निगरानी प्रणाली विकसित करना;
- नियमित प्रशिक्षण और विश्लेषणात्मक उपकरणों के माध्यम से PAC सचिवालयों एवं सदस्यों की क्षमता बढ़ाना;
- लंबित ऑडिट टिप्पणियों की समीक्षा के लिए PAC की हर माह कम से कम तीन बैठकें आयोजित करने और उप-समितियां गठित करने पर विचार करना;
- CAG के साथ समन्वय मजबूत कर उन्नत Forensic Tools के माध्यम से उच्च जोखिम वाले क्षेत्रों की पहचान और विधायी निगरानी सुनिश्चित करना; तथा विधायी प्रक्रियाओं की अखंडता और पवित्रता बनाए रखते हुए Digital Solutions का प्रभावी उपयोग करना।

हम इस resolution को आगे बढ़ाएंगे, ताकि वित्तीय प्रबंधन में बेहतर अनुशासन, पारदर्शिता और जवाबदेही सुनिश्चित की जा सके।

केवल बजट का बढ़ना किसी योजना की सफलता का प्रमाण नहीं है। योजना की वास्तविक सफलता तभी है, जब विधायिका नियमित रूप से निगरानी करे कि बजट में जिस मद के लिए धन निर्धारित किया गया था, उसका उपयोग उसी उद्देश्य के लिए हुआ है या नहीं।

मेरा मानना है कि हम सभी का दृष्टिकोण इस विषय पर एक समान है। हम अलग-अलग राजनीतिक दलों से हो सकते हैं, विचारधाराएं अलग-अलग हो सकती हैं, लेकिन हमारा साझा उद्देश्य वित्तीय अनुशासन, पारदर्शिता और जवाबदेही सुनिश्चित करना है।

मुझे पूरा विश्वास है कि दो दिनों तक इस कॉन्फ्रेंस में सभी प्रतिभागी सदस्यों को एक - दूसरे से सीखने को मिला होगा। साझे संकल्प को अपनाने के साथ ही यह सम्मेलन हमारी Public Accounts Committees को अधिक उन्नत, विकसित एवं सशक्त बनाने में निश्चय ही सहायक सिद्ध होगा।

title: Cabinet approves continuation of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs) for expeditious trial of cases of rape and POCSO (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences) Act for a further period of five years (FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31)
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 3:34PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister, has approved the continuation of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), including exclusive POCSO Courts, for a further period of five years i.e. from 01.04.2026 to 31.03.2031. The Scheme has a total financial outlay of Rs.3,788.04 crore (Central Share of Rs.2,353.15 crore and State/UT Share of Rs.1,434.89 crore). The Central Share will be funded from the Nirbhaya Fund.
The major features of the approved Scheme are as follows:
Continuation of the Scheme for five years i.e. from 01.04.2026 to 31.03.2031.
The Scheme has provision of operationalisation of 850 Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), including exclusive POCSO Courts, across various participating States/Union Territories.
Provision of dedicated Judicial Officer, Special Public Prosecutor and 6 support staff to facilitate expeditious disposal of pending cases relating to rape and offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012.
Provision of financial assistance to participating States/UTs for meeting the operational expenditure of FTSCs, in accordance with the CSS funding pattern.
Major impact:
The continuation of the Scheme is expected to have the following major impacts:
Providing Speedy Justice:
Ensuring faster trials and timely justice for victims of sexual offences.
Reducing Pending Cases:
Reducing the number of pending cases of Rape and POCSO Act cases.
Child-Friendly and Victim-Centric Environment:
The Scheme encourages establishment of Vulnerable Witness Deposition Centres (VWDCs) and child-friendly court spaces to facilitate victim testimonies without causing further distress.
Reduced inequality:
By prioritizing cases involving vulnerable groups (women and children), the scheme intends to reduce inequalities in access to justice.
Implementation strategy and targets:
The Scheme shall be implemented by the Department of Justice in coordination with the respective State Governments and UT Administrations. The key implementation strategies and targets are as follows:
Expansion of Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs):
Provision of expansion of FTSCs from the current 779 to 850 so that the coverage can extend in additional districts. This expansion shall be on the basis of case pendency data across all States and Union Territories.
Dedicated Legal Support:
Introduction of a specialized Special Public Prosecutor assigned exclusively to each FTSC to ensure speedy trials.
Optimized Court Staffing:
Allocation of one Judicial Officer and six support staff per FTSC to streamline administrative workload and facilitate expeditious disposal of old cases
.
Financial assistance:
Central assistance shall be provided to participating States/UTs in accordance with the approved funding pattern and prescribed guidelines.
Monitoring and evaluation:
The Department of Justice shall monitor the performance of FTSCs through the FTSC Dashboard, periodic progress reports, Expenditure Statements of the State. The Department shall also hold consultations with High Courts and State Governments and take their feedback for effective implementation of the Scheme.
Performance targets:
The Scheme aims to improve the rate of disposal of pending rape and POCSO Act cases, reduce case pendency and facilitate time-bound trials.
The primary beneficiaries of the Scheme are women and children who are victims of rape and offences under the POCSO Act, 2012.
The Scheme is proposed to be expanded to cover up to 850 FTSCs. This expansion is intended to include additional districts, which shall be identified on the basis of the pendency of rape and POCSO Act cases.
Background:
This Scheme has been operational since 02.10.2019. It has undergone successive extensions to ensure continuity of dedicated fast track courts for the expeditious disposal of rape and POCSO Act cases. The status of the Scheme is as follows:
Particulars
Date of launch
02.10.2019
Participating States/UTs
29
Total functional FTSCs including exclusive POCSO Courts
779 including 399 exclusive POCSO Courts
Total cases disposed of since inception of the Scheme
4,02,457
Proposed number of FTSCs under the extended Scheme
850
Approved continuation period
to 31.03.2031
The Scheme has contributed to strengthening the judicial response to the crime of sexual offences by providing dedicated courts for the disposal of rape and POCSO Act cases. The Department of Justice regularly monitors the functioning of FTSCs through the FTSC Dashboard, periodic data collection from High Courts and review meetings with concerned stakeholders. The continuation of the Scheme for another five years is expected to further strengthen the institutional capacity of the judiciary, reduce pendency of sexual offence cases and ensure timely justice to victims, particularly women and children.
The Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Fast Track Special Courts was launched on 02.10.2019 in pursuance of the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, and in compliance to the directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India dated 25.07.2019 in Suo Motu Writ (Criminal) No. 1/2019. The Hon'ble Supreme Court had directed for establishment of exclusive Special Courts in districts having more than 100 pending cases under the POCSO Act, 2012.
Accordingly, the Central Government launched the Scheme for establishing dedicated FTSCs, including exclusive POCSO Courts. The emphasis was on the time-bound disposal of pending cases relating to rape and offences under the POCSO Act, 2012.
The Scheme was initially launched for a period of one year and was subsequently extended up to 31.03.2026. The present approval ensures continuation of the Scheme for a further period of five years, i.e. up to 31.03.2031.

title: Cabinet approves ‘Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR)’, a central sector scheme for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 3:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today approved the ‘Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR)’ Scheme for the period FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31 with an outlay of Rs.4,371.10 crore.
Aligned with the central objective of Viksit Bharat 2047, the VISTAR Scheme is designed to establish a dynamic, real-time and future-ready official statistical architecture for enhanced timeliness, data granularity, interoperability with harmonised and AI ready datasets.
The VISTAR scheme will provide the strategic flexibility to dynamically allocate resources based on immediate policy needs, fostering a holistic approach to large-scale survey execution, methodological research, digital transformation, and national data governance. VISTAR Scheme will encompass all statistical and data management activities of MoSPI and it will play a crucial role for upgrading the official statistical system of the country. The three components of the VISTAR scheme are as follows:
Component 1: Comprehensive Statistical Operations and Strengthening of Ecosystem
Component 2: Support for Statistical Strengthening (SSS)
Component 3: Economic Census (EC)
Under the Comprehensive Statistical Operations and Strengthening of Ecosystem component, MoSPI proposes conducting 59 surveys during the 16th FC cycle, as compared to 43 major surveys conducted previously, potentially filling up critical data gaps in various sectors, thereby, improving decision-making and enabling timely and targeted policy interventions. In addition, building on recent digital transformations in technology enabled data collection and user-centric dissemination, MoSPI will focus on the end-to-end digitalization of statistical processes and embedding Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning into regular workflows, primarily for data processing, validation, and analysis.
MoSPI is planning to release new metrices, including the Headline Index of Services Production, the Index of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises. MoSPI will build upon the foundational pillars of data harmonisation such as data cataloguing, machine readability, interoperability, sharing protocols, and privacy by design etc. to dismantle silos and improve programme targeting, reduce duplication, and pave the way for AI-driven decision-making across government levels. By mainstreaming alternate sources—like mobile phone, scanner, and e-commerce data—MoSPI will aim to complement traditional surveys, reduce respondent burden, fill data gaps, and strengthen evidence-based policymaking. Furthermore, MoSPI will ensure capacity building and enhanced opportunities for youth and researchers through Internship Scheme for students and research proposals from academic & research institutions.
Under the Support for Statistical Strengthening (SSS) component, funds are to be provided to State/UT Governments for transforming the statistical capabilities of States and Union Territories through a redesigned, deliverable-linked framework (SSS 2.0). The vision focuses on building state-level capacity to generate high-quality, granular data at the district and other disaggregated levels, developing indigenous data processing capabilities, and embedding data use cases into localized policymaking. MoSPI will provide technical support to scale up generation of district-level estimates and million-plus city level estimates in flagship national surveys (e.g., PLFS, HCES, ASUSE) as well as in compilation of State/District level GDP and State level IIP.
Under the Economic Census (EC) component, MoSPI will undertake the 8th Economic Census (EC) in collaboration with the States / UTs which will provide granular data and activity details of all the non – farm establishments and workers hired, therein, upto Gram Panchayat and Ward level, providing an assessment of the unorganized sector of the economy and will serve as the baseline for developing National Statistical Business Register (SBR) to facilitate targeted enterprise surveys and strategic interventions. The economic census data will be extremely useful for planners and policy makers at national and sub-national levels, which will pave way for estimating the contribution of unorganized sector to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

title: Cabinet Approves Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing with an Outlay of Rs.2,814 Crore for Lithium and Nickel processing
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 3:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the ‘Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing’ with a financial outlay of Rs.2,814 crore over a period of five years.
Processing of critical minerals remains geographically concentrated in a few global locations. This exposes supply chains to geopolitical disruptions, price volatility, and potential supply restrictions, posing severe threats to supply chain resilience and economic security. This has implications for national security, economic sovereignty, and the timely achievement of decarbonisation targets.
At present, India remains substantially dependent on imports for refined intermediates and high-purity materials, owing to the nascent stage of domestic beneficiation and processing infrastructure for critical minerals, including Lithium, Nickel, Cobalt. Domestic processing capacity for critical minerals remains limited, with commercial-scale projects facing challenges relating to high capital requirements, limited availability of suitable technologies and constrained access to raw materials. Domestic processing capacity is therefore imperative for maximising value addition, achieving import substitution, and establishing resilient end-to-end value chains.
Against this backdrop, the “Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing” has been formulated to provide targeted capital expenditure support for the establishment and operationalisation of domestic processing facilities. The scheme aims to develop domestic processing capabilities in India to support value addition within the country, reduce import dependence, and develop value chain. The scheme targets processing of Lithium and Nickel ores/intermediary products into high purity compounds. Cobalt is also expected to be recovered as a by-product of nickel production. This will support critical sectors such as electric mobility, Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), electronics, defence, speciality steel etc.
The proposed scheme envisages a total financial outlay of Rs.2,814 crore. The scheme period is from FY 2026-27 to 2030-31. Under the scheme, capital subsidy of 30% of eligible investment will be provided for setting up four critical mineral processing plants, comprising two lithium processing plants (with a minimum capacity of 30 kt each) and two nickel processing plants (with a minimum capacity of 50 kt each). The maximum capital support will be capped at Rs.500 crore per lithium beneficiary and Rs.900 crore per nickel beneficiary, respectively.
The selection of beneficiaries shall be carried out through a two-stage process. In the first stage, applications shall be assessed for technical qualification, and only technically qualified applicants shall be eligible to participate in the second stage of financial bidding. For each mineral, two beneficiaries shall be selected based on the least-cost criterion, i.e., the lowest CAPEX support sought by the bidders under the Scheme. The incentives will be disbursed in three tranches linked to the achievement of specified milestones.
The Scheme is an important step towards advancing the objectives of Atmanirbhar Bharat by supporting the development of resilient domestic processing infrastructure and strengthening India’s capabilities across the critical mineral value chain.

title: Cabinet approves Rs.14,500 crore Viability Gap Funding Scheme for development of 92 GWh Grid-Scale Energy Storage Systems
subtitle:
Scheme to support 30 GWh Battery Energy Storage Systems, 60 GWh Pumped Storage Projects and 2 GWh emerging storage technologies

Will accelerate renewable energy integration, strengthen grid stability and ensure reliable and affordable round-the-clock power supply

Mandatory domestic content requirement for BESS to promote indigenous manufacturing and reduce import dependence
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 3:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) Scheme for Development of Grid-Scale Energy Storage Systems, with a total financial support of Rs.14,500 crore for the period FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. The scheme aims to support the development of 92 GWh of, yet to be commissioned; energy storage capacity across the country. The scheme will support creation of new capacities equivalent to 170% of the present-day Grid Scale Energy Storage System capacity in the country and help meet the required Grid Scale ESS capacity of 411 GWh by 2031-32.
The scheme marks a significant step towards strengthening India's power sector infrastructure, facilitating large-scale integration of renewable energy and ensuring reliable, affordable and round-the-clock power supply. It will also provide an impetus to domestic manufacturing of battery energy storage systems, reduce import dependence and enhance the country's long-term energy security.
The scheme envisages the development of 60 GWh of Hydro Pumped Storage Plant (PSP) capacity, 30 GWh of Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity and 2 GWh of capacity through alternative energy storage technologies, with a total estimated investment of Rs.97,600 crore. The VGF support will help improve the financial viability of these projects and accelerate the deployment of large-scale energy storage infrastructure in the country.
Energy storage capacity will be allocated through a tariff-based competitive bidding process. Public and private sector electricity distribution companies will be eligible for VGF support for BESS and Hydro PSP projects, while projects based on alternative energy storage technologies will be implemented by public and private sector entities.
A key objective of the scheme is to strengthen India's domestic energy storage manufacturing ecosystem through demand-side financial support and reduce dependence on imported components. To promote indigenous manufacturing, BESS projects will be subject to a minimum Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) of 40%. The requirement will encourage domestic manufacturing, create opportunities for Indian industry and complement existing supply-side incentives for battery manufacturing.
The scheme represents an important intervention towards building a flexible, resilient and future-ready electricity system. By accelerating the deployment of grid-scale energy storage, it will facilitate greater utilisation of renewable energy, address the variability of renewable energy generation and reduce dependence on conventional generation for meeting balancing round-the clock power supply. The initiative will strengthen grid stability, improve renewable energy integration, encourage domestic manufacturing and enhance India's energy security, while advancing the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, has called upon citizens to make health and preventive healthcare an integral part of Dhanteras celebrations, emphasising that true prosperity lies in good health and well-being. Highlighting the significance of the festival, the Minister encouraged families to adopt healthier lifestyle practices, prioritise disease prevention and make conscious investments in their long-term health.
Dhanteras, also associated with Dhanvantari Jayanti, commemorates the emergence of Lord Dhanvantari during the Samudra Manthan, carrying the Amrit Kalash. Revered as the divine physician of the gods, Lord Dhanvantari is closely associated with Ayurveda, India's traditional science of life and health. The occasion offers an opportunity to reflect on the importance of health as the foundation of individual and family prosperity.
Shri Jadhav highlighted that while Dhanteras is traditionally associated with purchasing gold, silver and household items as symbols of prosperity, the festival also serves as a reminder that material wealth holds greater value when accompanied by good health. He emphasised that families should give as much importance to safeguarding their health as they do to securing their future prosperity.
Drawing attention to the importance of preventive healthcare, the Minister observed that healthcare discussions often begin after an illness has developed, whereas equal emphasis must be placed on preventing diseases through healthy lifestyle choices. Referring to the Ayurvedic principle
“Swasthasya Swasthya Rakshanam”
,
which emphasises the preservation of the health of healthy individuals, he highlighted the relevance of this approach in addressing growing challenges such as non-communicable diseases, sedentary lifestyles and stress.
The Minister underscored that everyday habits, including balanced nutrition, regular physical activity, adequate sleep and stress management, play an important role in maintaining overall well-being. He encouraged families to promote home-cooked and nutritious food, reduce excessive consumption of junk food, undertake regular physical activities and ensure that elderly family members receive appropriate care and attention. Regular yoga practice and timely health screenings were also highlighted as important steps towards preventive healthcare.
Highlighting the contribution of Ayush systems in promoting preventive and promotive healthcare, Shri Jadhav noted that initiatives such as Ayushman Arogya Mandirs are helping expand access to Ayush-based healthcare services at the community level. He also emphasised the importance of scientific research, quality standards and evidence-based practices to ensure that India's traditional systems of medicine contribute responsibly to the country's healthcare framework.
Referring to the Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of a Fit India, the Minister recalled his emphasis on bringing small but meaningful changes to everyday lifestyles to help prevent lifestyle-related diseases. He highlighted that fitness is not merely an individual pursuit but an essential foundation for a healthy and prosperous society. As India moves towards the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, healthier and more health-conscious citizens will be central to the country's development journey.
Calling upon citizens to make preventive healthcare a personal and family commitment this Dhanteras, Shri Jadhav encouraged everyone to introduce at least one positive health habit into their daily routine and motivate another family member to do the same. He also urged people to pay greater attention to the health of elderly family members, women and children, seek timely medical advice and make healthy living a shared family responsibility.
The Minister emphasised that this Dhanteras, citizens should look beyond traditional symbols of prosperity and embrace healthier habits, care for their loved ones and make preventive healthcare the foundation of their families' future, reaffirming the timeless principle that
“Health is the Greatest Wealth.”

title: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal inaugurates Vanijya Bhawan and Udyog Bhawan in Jaipur
subtitle:
Jaipur becomes the first city to house all departments and affiliated offices of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry at one location

Shri Goyal calls for co-location of offices of all 46 organisations under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry across the country

Co-location to create one-stop centres for promoting exports, investments and internal trade, and facilitating businesses

Shri Piyush Goyal reiterates commitment to citizen-centric governance, says serving citizens is the Government's foremost responsibility
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today virtually inaugurated Vanijya Bhawan and Udyog Bhawan in Jaipur, marking the beginning of the co-location of offices of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and its associated and affiliated organisations at a single location. Jaipur has become the first city and the first State capital to bring all these offices together under one roof.
Congratulating the Departments of Commerce and Departments for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) on the initiative, Shri Goyal said that the project should mark the beginning of rapid action towards implementing the concept across the country, particularly in every State capital. He said that these centres would serve as hubs to support industry and international trade and function as one-stop locations for activities relating to the promotion of exports, investments and internal trade. They would also support businesses and industry in their journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047.
Emphasising that the initiative must become a collective commitment of the entire ecosystem, Shri Goyal called for the active participation of government offices, stakeholders, State Government representatives, exporters, importers, investors and businesses. He stressed that the objective should go beyond administrative consolidation and extend to transforming service delivery, simplifying processes and making it easier to do business and comply with the laws of the land.
The Minister directed that all processes, including applications for licences and permits, SCOMET approvals and other services, should move entirely online. He set 31st March 2027 as the deadline for completing the necessary digitisation, including the digitisation of past data and records at the Regional Authorities (RAs) of the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) across the country. From 1st April 2027, no person should be required or expected to visit any of the offices physically for these services.
He said that, wherever physical verification of original documents is necessary, a small counter could be provided to facilitate verification and uploading of documents. Computers could also be installed at office entrances to enable simultaneous verification and uploading of documents, wherever required. The Minister encouraged self-certification and greater trust in stakeholders, stressing that the Government should demonstrate its confidence in citizens and businesses.
Shri Goyal also called for the simplification of processes, formats and forms, and urged the departments to break organisational silos and work collectively to deliver better outcomes for businesses and citizens. He said that improved coordination between the two departments and the various organisations under the Ministry would be essential to achieving the objectives of the initiative.
The Minister informed that the Ministry currently has around 500 offices and 46 organisations. Except for very large campuses, such as the large office of ECGC in Mumbai, which would continue to function independently, the other offices would be brought under the co-location arrangement. He clarified that the co-located centres would not provide services only for the organisations physically situated there but would facilitate services across all 46 organisations and different departments under the Ministry.
He said that even where officials of a particular organisation were not physically stationed at a co-located office, people would be encouraged to interact with them through video conferencing. Accordingly, Shri Goyal directed that adequate video conferencing facilities be provided at every co-located office, with the provision to expand them to two or three counters depending on the size and requirements of the office.
The Minister emphasised that these centres should increasingly function as facilitation and promotion offices. Their role would be to promote investments and foreign trade, assist people seeking guidance, attract investments into India, encourage capital expenditure in the country and promote exports. He clarified that their purpose should not be limited to facilitating the issuance of licences.
Shri Goyal said that the co-location of offices, digitisation and introduction of faceless assessments would enhance transparency, accountability and public confidence. A unified presence of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry in each State would assure businesses and stakeholders that they could access support and guidance through a single location.
Highlighting the importance of efficient service delivery amid considerable uncertainty and volatility in international trade and global geopolitical affairs, the Minister said that time was of the essence and competitiveness was crucial for success. He called upon officials to ensure that the functioning of every office was facilitative, supportive, friendly and helpful. He added that bringing offices together under one roof would also help establish checks and balances in their functioning.
The Minister directed that every office be equipped with CCTV cameras connected to a central server in Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi, to enable random monitoring of work being undertaken across the country. He clarified that the objective was not continuous monitoring but periodic checks to oversee functioning and provide protection against theft and other such incidents.
He further directed that all offices must possess the necessary approvals required for their functioning, including Fire Brigade approvals and approvals under the Shops and Establishments Act. Emphasising the importance of workplace facilities, he said that every office must have high-quality toilets for men and women, with multi-gender facilities wherever appropriate in smaller offices. All offices must also have accessible toilets for persons with disabilities. He stressed that the quality of these facilities should be at least at par with, and preferably better than, those at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi, and directed that adequate resources be allocated for this purpose.
Shri Goyal also emphasised that furniture and equipment should be modular wherever possible and that all procurement, including furniture, equipment, lighting and curtains, should be domestic or Swadeshi, except where absolutely unavoidable.
The Minister urged officials to examine opportunities for further reducing timelines and introducing deemed approvals wherever feasible. He called upon the Secretaries, Additional Secretaries and Joint Secretaries to regularly conduct video conferences or hybrid meetings with stakeholders across different regions. He also stressed the need to continuously identify ways to reduce paperwork and make it easier for people to obtain services and outcomes from the Ministry's offices.
Shri Goyal said that the initiative would strengthen teamwork within the two departments and among various internal and external stakeholders, improve coordination between different wings of the Ministry and enhance overall operational efficiency. It would help the Ministry become more contemporary and modern while preparing it for its role in the journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047.
Highlighting the expanding responsibilities of the Ministry in the context of several new trade agreements and the opening up of new markets, the Minister said that India had emerged as a bold, confident and unstoppable economy on the global stage. He emphasised the need to prepare the country for the goal of becoming a USD 30 trillion economy by 2047.
Reiterating that the fundamental responsibility of the Ministry was to serve the people and businesses of India, Shri Goyal said that, as Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has emphasised, the citizen is like God and the Government's responsibility is to serve citizens with that spirit.

title: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) Launches Network Anubhav Platform
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 4:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today launched the Network Anubhav Platform – A geospatial and analytical dashboard for user test data and TRAI independent drive test data and to provide DND web interface. User test data comprises of the test results from MySpeed and MyCall apps of TRAI. The platform delivers insights on various network parameters to consumers, service providers and TRAI.
Key Features of the Geo-Spatial Maps
Geo-Spatial maps allow consumers to:-
View test results categorised as Cellular or Fixed broadband, further segregated service provider-wise and technology-wise, based on parameters, including download and upload speeds.
Navigate and zoom the map to examine the location and distribution of consumer-generated test observations.
Use filters, legends, supporting tables and downloadable reports to interpret the displayed results.
The platform reports percentile values calculated from tests conducted by users in a given area:
P50 (median speed):
Half of the tests recorded a speed at or above this value.
P80 (for Mobile Broadband):
80% of the tests recorded a speed at or above this value.
P90 (for Fixed Broadband):
90% of the tests recorded a speed at or above this value.
Though these values based on user tests do not represent comprehensive assessment of network quality based on standard methodology, they provide valuable information to users regarding experience of other users at various locations. The maps also facilitate a geospatial appreciation of independent drive tests for various locations. Together, these data sets and their geospatial visualization provide valuable information to users about experience of other users and results of Independent Drive Tests.
Empowerment of Consumers
Consumers can report spam and test internet speeds. Aggregated results from TRAI Apps, web interface, and Independent Drive Tests are available on the Network Anubhav dashboard. Consumers can view location-specific results of tests conducted by other users.
Insights for TSPs and TRAI
Through a secure interface, Telecom service providers can view data of call quality, coverage and internet tests conducted by consumers. Along with location, date, time, and values of technical parameters, TSPs can identify geographic locations for further analysis and can use it for network improvement.
TRAI can use the aggregated insights for evidence-based monitoring of consumer experience and use this data for improvement in network performance.
MySpeed SDK
TRAI's MySpeed SDK enables eligible third-party apps to integrate connectivity-measurement capabilities. Wider integration can expand participation and the volume of real-world measurements contributing to the platform.
DND Services
With Anubhav portal access to the DND is now available through web interface. Consumers can use the available DND facilities to exercise preference for commercial communication, submit complaints relating to unsolicited commercial communication, track complaint status and view consolidated and service-provider-wise complaint information.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Anil Kumar Lahoti, Chairman, TRAI, said:
“The Network Anubhav Platform brings greater transparency to observed network tests conducted by Consumers and TRAI. It empowers consumers to analyse location and service provider specific tests, enables TSPs to identify areas for network optimisation and strengthens TRAI’s efforts for network improvement.”
Consumers are encouraged to contribute regularly through the TRAI MySpeed and MyCall apps. Wider participation will improve the coverage and utility of the platform’s information.
Access the Platform
Network Anubhav portal: https://anubhav.trai.gov.in
For additional queries, please contact: Ms. Archna Ahlawat, Advisor (IT), at
advisorit@trai.gov.in
.

title: Supply chain diversification & greater regional cooperation are key to stronger maritime inter-dependence amid strained security environment: Raksha Mantri at Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue 2026
subtitle:
“Certain actors & nations seek to exploit the criticality of oceans for narrow unilateral gains; Answer to interconnected world’s vulnerabilities lies in building resilience”

Maritime security must evolve with emerging threats; Leveraging emerging technologies is the need of the hour, says Shri Rajnath Singh

“Technology must not become another source of inequality among nations; Benefits to a few won’t achieve collective resilience”

“Economic development & environmental responsibility must progress together; Oceans cannot be treated as unlimited source of resources”

“Maritime sector to be a key driver of India’s Viksit Bharat journey; Govt striving to develop a comprehensive maritime ecosystem”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 5:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called for making inter-dependence among regional partners more secure and resilient through diversification of supply chains, reliable maritime infrastructure, enhanced maritime awareness and greater cooperation, along with the ability to anticipate, withstand and recover from disruptions, amid growing strains in the global maritime security environment. He was delivering the commemorative address at the Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue (IPRD), the Indian Navy’s annual apex-level international strategic conference, being held in New Delhi on November 4, 2026.
Describing oceans as bridges rather than barriers among nations & civilisations, Raksha Mantri highlighted their role in sustaining livelihoods and facilitating the exchange of goods, knowledge & culture. He stated that despite the international community's awareness of these universal dependencies, certain actors and nations seek to exploit the criticality of the oceans for narrow unilateral gains. “The global maritime security environment is strained by deliberate trade disruptions. We see blatant challenges to the freedom of navigation and the weaponisation of narrow maritime passages. This growing instability in the maritime domain casts a long shadow over the broader international order,” he added.
Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that the answer to the vulnerabilities of an interconnected world lies in building resilience, emphasising that globalisation cannot be abandoned in response to every disruption, nor should maritime spaces that have enabled human progress be closed. He stressed that the objective must be to make inter-dependence more secure.
Highlighting the evolving nature of maritime security, Raksha Mantri stated that challenges could arise not only from conventional military activities but also from non-traditional threats such as piracy, trafficking, illegal fishing, cyber-attacks and natural disasters. He underscored the need for maritime security to evolve with the changing maritime domain. “Artificial intelligence is changing the way data is processed, while autonomous systems are expanding the possibilities of surveillance & operations. New sensors are improving our ability to observe the oceans. Advances in materials, biotechnology and data analytics are opening new avenues for research and application. These developments have enormous implications for maritime security and economic activity. But technology, by itself, is not the answer. The more important question is how we use technology to address real challenges,” he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh also underlined that technology must not become another source of inequality among nations as the Indo-Pacific includes countries with different levels of technological and economic capability. “Some possess advanced research infrastructure. Others are still developing the institutional and human resources required to participate fully in this transformation. If technological progress benefits only a limited number of countries, we will not achieve the collective resilience that our region requires,” he said.
Raksha Mantri called for promoting cooperation in research, education, innovation and capacity building, stating that a stronger scientific capability in one country can contribute to the security & prosperity of the entire region. Terming it particularly important for smaller maritime nations and developing countries, he said the most useful technology is not necessarily the most expensive or sophisticated; it is the one that solves a real problem.
Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised that as India moves towards Viksit Bharat by 2047, the maritime domain will play a crucial role in the country’s national transformation. He highlighted Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi-led Government’s efforts to develop a comprehensive maritime ecosystem through investments in port infrastructure and connectivity, port-led development under Sagarmala, promotion of coastal economic activities and strengthening of the maritime industrial base. He described the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 as the national blueprint for this transformation, with emphasis on technology, innovation, research, education and skills.
Raksha Mantri underlined the need for economic development and environmental responsibility to progress together, stating that oceans cannot be treated as an unlimited source of resources. He advocated the protection of marine ecosystems, responsible utilisation of ocean resources and placing the interests of coastal communities at the centre of development efforts. “National prosperity and ecological responsibility are not competing objectives. They must reinforce each other,” he said.
Reaffirming India's commitment to an open, inclusive and rule-based maritime order, Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) that recognises the interconnected nature of security and prosperity among nations and underscores that the maritime future of the Indo-Pacific cannot be shaped by any single country acting alone. He also termed the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative, announced by PM Modi in 2019, as a practical framework for advancing maritime cooperation across seven interconnected areas.
Emphasising the need to translate regional cooperation into tangible outcomes, the Raksha Mantri urged the participants of IPRD to move beyond identifying challenges and focus on practical action. He pitched for stronger scientific networks, joint research, exchanges between universities and maritime institutions, and the development of affordable technological solutions to common challenges. Stressing that the deliberations at the IPRD must lead to concrete outcomes, he said ideas emerging from the dialogue must translate into partnerships, projects and measurable outcomes.
“The future of the Indo Pacific will not be shaped by technology alone. It will be shaped by the wisdom with which we use that technology, the partnerships we build and the confidence we create among nations,” Shri Rajnath Singh said, reiterating India's readiness to contribute to this collective endeavour.
Raksha Mantri expressed hope that the deliberations would lead to meaningful discussions and practical cooperation. He concluded with a call to move “from shared challenges to shared understanding. From shared understanding to shared knowledge. And from shared knowledge to shared resilience and shared prosperity.”
In his address, Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS) highlighted the interconnected nature of the oceans and the uneven distribution of scientific knowledge, research infrastructure and technological capabilities across the Indo-Pacific. He emphasised that maritime cooperation must extend beyond equipment acquisition to building sustainable capabilities, enabling partner nations to operate, maintain, adapt and upgrade technologies.
Underscoring the need for a broader and more integrated approach to maritime challenges, the CNS called for greater collective investment in ocean science and research, enhanced sharing of scientific data and technology, and collaborative research initiatives, including joint scientific expeditions. He also highlighted the importance of strengthening existing regional institutions and mechanisms through trust, transparency and inclusive ocean governance.
The CNS observed that IPRD-2026 provides an important platform for translating shared maritime interests into practical outcomes and generating concrete, forward-looking recommendations to strengthen science, technology and academic cooperation across the Indo-Pacific
Also among the dignitaries present were Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, former CNS and Chairman, NMF Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi (Retd).
The three-day IPRD 2026, being conducted by the Indian Navy in association with the National Maritime Foundation (NMF), commenced on November 3, 2026. The second day of the dialogue focused upon two closely connected issues of regional maritime resilience: a better shared understanding of activities at sea and a stronger scientific capacity to anticipate and respond to environmental change.
The day also witnessed a ministerial session featuring a special address by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences Dr Jitendra Singh. He also released an NMF publication titled ‘Alternative Hull Forms for the Future Indian Navy’.
Adding a Naval perspective to the overarching theme of IPRD 2026, an interactive session ‘Perspectives from the Flag Bridge’ brought together former Indian Navy chiefs Admiral RK Dhowan, Admiral Sunil Lanba, Admiral Karambir Singh and Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi, and former Commander of the Sri Lanka Navy, Admiral Jayantha Perera, in a conversation hosted by Director General, NMF Vice Admiral Pradeep Chauhan. This session offered invaluable insights on the relationship between maritime strategy, technological change and regional cooperation, with a specific reference to naval cooperation under the aegis of the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium, which is currently being chaired by the Indian Navy.
In addition, a session, moderated by Commodore Abhinav Barve, Indian Navy, focused upon ‘Oceanographic Science and Climate Resilience’. In this session, the speakers deliberated upon the scientific foundations of regional preparedness with special emphasis on cooperative maritime networks for climate resilience in Indian Ocean Island States such as Mauritius and Seychelles.  The aspects of translation of ocean science into policy and collaborative sharing of ocean data, including cooperation involving research vessels, observation networks, forecasting capabilities and appropriate data-sharing arrangements, were also addressed during this session.
The two ministerial sessions on the second day of IPRD 2026 lent strategic guidance to the conference and offered a holistic perspective on India’s collaborative approach in addressing maritime security concerns in the Indo-Pacific.

title: India Aiming for Global Competitiveness Through Indigenous Capabilities and International Cooperation: Dr. Jitendra Singh at IPRD 2026
subtitle:
India’s First Human Deep-Sea Mission to Reach Depths of Up to 6,000 Metres by 2028, Alongside Progress in Gaganyaan Mission

Deep Ocean Resources to Be a Major Source of Economic Value Addition for Achieving Viksit Bharat 2047: Dr. Jitendra Singh

‘One Ocean, Shared Knowledge and Equitable Prosperity’ Should Guide Indo-Pacific Cooperation: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh

Prime Minister’s Reference to Deep Ocean Mission in Independence Day Addresses Reflects Strategic Priority to Ocean Resources: Dr. Jitendra Singh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India is aiming to achieve global competitiveness in ocean research and exploration through indigenous capabilities, international cooperation and global co-creation, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, said while addressing the Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue (IPRD) 2026, organised by the National Maritime Foundation under the Ministry of Defence.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India's approach to scientific missions in recent years has increasingly been based on a mission-mode framework, bringing together multiple departments and institutions rather than confining research to individual ministries. He highlighted the growing convergence of ocean sciences, space technology, nuclear science, geology, electronics and robotics in advancing India's maritime and deep-ocean capabilities.
Highlighting India's indigenous capabilities in deep-ocean exploration, the Minister said that the National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai, has developed the capability to conduct trials at depths of 5,000 to 6,000 metres in the Central Indian Ocean Basin. He also referred to the Ocean Mineral Explorer, which enables high-resolution exploration of hydrothermal sulphide deposits, several of which have already been identified.He noted that the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi reference to the Deep Ocean Mission twice in his Independence Day addresses reflects the priority accorded to ocean resources at the highest level and their strategic importance for India's future.
Referring to the Samudrayaan Mission, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the
Matsya
submersible is designed to carry three aquanauts to depths of 5,000–6,000 metres. He said that India is progressing towards sending its first human deep-sea mission to a depth of up to 6,000 metres by 2028, marking an important milestone in the country's indigenous deep-ocean exploration programme.
Drawing a parallel with India's human spaceflight programme, the Minister said that the country is working towards a remarkable convergence of deep-sea and space exploration. He expressed the vision of having an Indian human being undertake a deep-sea journey to nearly 6,000 metres while almost simultaneously another Indian travels into space, reflecting the country's growing scientific and technological capabilities.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India's ocean research is increasingly supported by space-based capabilities. He referred to dedicated satellites contributing to ocean-related research through observations of ocean colour, sea-surface temperature and wind vectors. These capabilities, he said, are expanding the scope of ocean observation and could also support future exploration of renewable energy resources from the oceans, including wind and solar energy.
Emphasising the importance of a whole-of-government and whole-of-science approach, the Minister highlighted the contribution of different scientific institutions and departments to India's ocean-related missions. He referred to the role of nuclear technology in seawater desalination, including the desalination plant at Kalpakkam established with the support of Bhabha Atomic Research Centre and the low-temperature desalination facility in Lakshadweep developed through the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
The Minister said these initiatives demonstrate how different scientific disciplines and technologies can work together to address national requirements, including access to potable water in coastal and island regions.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that international cooperation would be equally important in advancing ocean research, as oceans do not follow political boundaries drawn by countries. Issues such as marine pollution and changes in ocean temperature have consequences extending across national jurisdictions, making collective scientific efforts essential.
The Minister called for global strategies and partnerships based on joint scientific missions, reciprocal access to research facilities and data sharing. He said India's approach should be guided by the principle of “One Ocean, Shared Knowledge and Equitable Prosperity”, with the diversity of histories, cultures and geographies across the Indo-Pacific serving as an opportunity to strengthen cooperation.
The Minister outlined key priorities for strengthening regional cooperation, including closing observational gaps and improving the forecasting of extreme events; establishing regional climate services partnerships for coasts and islands; promoting responsible and accessible ocean technologies; advancing deep-ocean research; and strengthening conservation and equitable use of ocean resources.
Highlighting the role of research and innovation funding, Dr. Jitendra Singh referred to the establishment of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation and the announcement of the ₹1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund to accelerate private-sector participation in research and development.
Dr Jitendra Singh said the RDI Fund provides for a 50:50 equity-based approach, encouraging private-sector stakeholders and investors to participate alongside the government in emerging areas of research and technology. He emphasised that government departments, scientific institutions, private-sector stakeholders and investors must work together to develop new sectors and strengthen India's technological capabilities.
Connecting ocean exploration with the national vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, the Minister said that achieving the country's development goals would require identifying new sources of economic value addition. He observed that a significant part of this potential lies in resources that remain unexplored or underexplored, with the deep ocean representing one of the major opportunities.
During the interaction with participants, Dr. Jitendra Singh also addressed a question on the potential of nuclear-powered vessels and the future of clean energy in maritime transport. He referred to the recent opening of the nuclear sector to private participation under the SHANTI Act and India's target of achieving 100 GW of nuclear energy capacity by 2047. He said that the Deep Ocean Mission is also exploring different possibilities for generating renewable energy from the oceans, including through solar panels, ocean winds and temperature or energy gradients.
Responding to a suggestion on extending the Swachh Bharat initiative to the oceans, the Minister said that the government had already initiated an annual ocean-cleanliness campaign. Recalling its beginning during the commemoration of 75 years of Independence, he said the initiative had since developed into an annual effort involving coastal district administrations, the Indian Navy, the Indian Coast Guard, NGOs and other stakeholders. He emphasised that marine pollution cannot remain confined to one country and that efforts towards cleaner oceans would benefit the wider Indo-Pacific region.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India's growing indigenous capabilities, combined with international partnerships and responsible sharing of scientific knowledge, would be crucial to strengthening its role in global ocean research and exploration. He called upon stakeholders to work collectively towards the peaceful, sustainable and equitable use of ocean resources, contributing to the national vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

title: Union Environment Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav releases Guidelines for Designation of India’s Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (I-OECMs), 2026, at CBD COP-17 in Yerevan, Armenia
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 7:15PM by PIB Chennai
content:
The Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, released the “Guidelines for the designation of India’s Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (I-OECMs) 2026” at a side event of the 17th Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP-17) in Yerevan, Armenia on 03 November 2026. The event, titled “From Policy to Practice: Advancing India’s Biodiversity Commitments through Innovation, Finance, ABS and OECMs”, was organised by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). The Minister of Environment of Armenia and the Executive Secretary, CBD joined in the release.
Minister has stated that, “OECMs is the new era of conservation approach where effective in-situ conservation of biodiversity is achieved mainly through effective landscape management lying outside forests and protected areas”.
The Guidelines have been prepared by MoEFCC in partnership with NBA. They provide a framework for recognising and reporting areas outside the legally protected and conserved areas that deliver positive and sustained long-term outcomes for the
in-situ
conservation of biodiversity. The initiative supports India’s implementation of Target 3 (30x30) of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KM-GBF) and of National Biodiversity Target 3 under the updated National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP, 2024–2030).
The Guidelines cover terrestrial, inland water, and coastal and marine ecosystems. Illustrative sites include biodiversity parks, sacred groves, community-managed irrigation tanks, seagrass and seaweed beds, and fisheries seasonal ban areas. Four criteria are mandatory for recognition. The area must not be a legally protected or conserved area, and it must be governed and managed under Central or State Government frameworks or by government-recognised local institutions such as Panchayats and Biodiversity Management Committees. It must also have defined boundaries and must not overlap with any area already reported to the World Database on Protected Areas. Finally, recognition must not alter the existing activities, governance or regulatory regime of the area. Sites may additionally qualify on the strength of their biodiversity significance and their ecosystem services and cultural values.
Applications may be submitted to NBA by Central and State Government departments, agencies and institutions, local self-governments and Biodiversity Management Committees. NBA will conduct a preliminary examination and forward each application to the concerned State Biodiversity Board or Union Territory Biodiversity Council within 30 days. The Board or Council will validate the information and send its recommendation to NBA within 30 days. With the support of an Inter-Departmental I-OECM Committee, NBA will take the final decision in coordination with MoEFCC, which will authorise recognition. Each recognised site must have a monitoring framework with measurable indicators, assessed at least once every five years, and State Biodiversity Boards/Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs) will maintain records of the sites in their States. MoEFCC and NBA will liaise with UNEP-WCMC to publish recognised sites on the World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas.
The Guidelines also provide for capacity-building programmes by NBA, SBBs/(UTBCs) and line departments, and for non-monetary recognition of good practices. I-OECM recognition does not make an area a protected area and does not change its ownership or legal status.
The Government of India has also commissioned a GEF-8 Project to implement these Guidelines in six demonstration landscapes and seascapes. The project is titled
“Enhancing the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity to meet India’s commitment to the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework targets by 2030”
. It is being executed by NBA and MoEFCC, under the National Implementation Modality, with support from UNDP, and was approved by the Local Project Appraisal Committee on 29 December 2025. The project runs for 72 months, from 15 May 2026 to 15 May 2032. Its total financing is USD 60.79 million, comprising a GEF Trust Fund grant of USD 6.65 million and confirmed co-financing of USD 54.14 million.
The project aims to add 3 per cent of India’s land and marine area to the country’s conservation estate, over and above the existing 27 per cent under protection, through OECMs and other conservation initiatives, including community and private conservation areas. It is structured around five components: an enabling framework for expanding and strengthening the conservation network; financing, incentives and capacities for operationalising OECMs; increased coverage and management effectiveness of the conservation network; knowledge management; and monitoring and evaluation. The six demonstration sites are the Gori Valley in Uttarakhand, the Kumbhalgarh–Mount Abu–Jaisalmer landscape in Rajasthan, the Satkosia–Kalahandi landscape in Odisha, the Srisailam–Cumbum landscape in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, the Sahyadri–Konkan landscape in Maharashtra and Goa, and the Lakshadweep Islands Marinescape.
The project aims to establish 50,000 hectares of new terrestrial conservation areas. It will also restore at least 5,000 hectares of degraded land and directly benefit at least 50,000 people, half of them women. It will further establish State-level OECM coordination mechanisms, a monitoring, reporting and verification system. Together, the Guidelines and the Project will help translate India’s commitment under the KM-GBF into recognised conservation sites on the ground.

The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC),  under the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Ministry of Finance, Government of India, has successfully concluded the second phase of the e-auction of land parcels belonging to Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), the corporate entity operating Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, on 3 November 2026.
The successful completion of the second phase marks another significant milestone in NLMC's efforts to facilitate the monetisation of surplus public assets through a structured, transparent, competitive and technology-enabled auction process.
The auction resulted in the successful sale of 114 land parcels, generating a total successful bid value of ₹218 crore, against an aggregate reserve price of ₹184.8 crore. The successful bids achieved an overall premium of 17.96% over the aggregate reserve price, demonstrating competitive bidding and effective market-driven price discovery.
The highest successful bid price recorded during the second phase was ₹182,650 per square yard, while the highest premium over the reserve price for an individual plot stood at 67.65%.
The results highlight sustained market interest in well-located land parcels in Visakhapatnam and demonstrate the effectiveness of a transparent and competitive e-auction mechanism in unlocking the economic value of surplus public assets.
Strong Performance Across Both Phases of RINL Land E-Auction
In the first phase, NLMC successfully auctioned 150 land parcels, generating a total successful bid value of ₹366.33 crore, against an aggregate reserve price of ₹312.48 crore. The successful bids recorded an average premium of 17.23% over the reserve price, with the highest auction price exceeding ₹1.80 lakh per square yard.
With the completion of both phases, a total of 264 land parcels have been successfully auctioned, generating an aggregate successful bid value of ₹584.33 crore, against a combined reserve price of ₹497.29 crore.

title: Union Health Ministry Proposes Immediate Suspension of Manufacturing Licences for Drugs Found Not of Standard Quality on Specified Critical Parameters
subtitle:
Proposed Amendments to Drugs Rules, 1945 Aim to Strengthen Regulatory Oversight and Ensure Prompt Action Against Substandard Medicines

Manufacturing Licences of Drugs Found Deficient in Assay, Dissolution, Related Substances, Impurities or Sterility Proposed to be Suspended Immediately

Restoration of Suspended Licences to be Permitted Only After Verified Corrective and Preventive Action by Manufacturers

Enhanced Reporting Mechanism Proposed to Facilitate Timely Regulatory Coordination and Strengthen Accountability
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 8:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant step towards strengthening the regulatory framework for ensuring the quality and safety of medicines in the country, the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to provide for immediate suspension of manufacturing licences in respect of drugs declared Not of Standard Quality (NSQ) on specified critical quality parameters.
The proposed amendments seek to enable prompt regulatory intervention upon detection of substandard medicines, prevent their continued manufacture and distribution, and strengthen the mechanism for ensuring compliance with prescribed quality standards, in the interest of patient safety and public health.
Under the existing provisions of the Drugs Rules, 1945
, suspension or cancellation of a manufacturing licence is preceded by the prescribed regulatory procedure, including issuance of a show-cause notice. This may result in a time gap between the declaration of a drug as NSQ and initiation of regulatory action. During this period, the concerned drug may continue to remain in circulation, posing potential risks to public health and making effective recall more challenging.
To address this regulatory concern, the Ministry has proposed a provision for immediate suspension of the manufacturing licence of the concerned drug by the Central Licensing Approving Authority or the State Licensing Authority, as the case may be, upon receipt of a Government Analyst's report declaring the drug as NSQ with respect to Assay, Dissolution, Related Substances, Impurities or Sterility.
These parameters are critical to determining the quality of medicines. The proposed provision aims to ensure that instances of non-compliance involving these specified parameters are met with prompt regulatory action, thereby minimising potential risks to patients.
The proposed amendment also provides for mandatory corrective measures before revocation of the suspension.
The suspension shall continue until the manufacturer undertakes an effective Root Cause Analysis to identify the reasons for the quality failure and implements appropriate Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) to the satisfaction of the concerned Licensing Authority.
Revocation of the suspension shall be permitted only after implementation of the requisite corrective and preventive measures and their due verification by the Licensing Authority. This mechanism is intended to ensure that identified quality deficiencies are adequately addressed and necessary safeguards are put in place to prevent their recurrence.
To further strengthen regulatory coordination and facilitate timely action
, consequential amendments have also been proposed to Form 13, relating to the test report of the Government Analyst.
Under the proposed mechanism, the Government Analyst's report would be endorsed to the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI), the concerned State/UT Licensing Authority under whose jurisdiction the manufacturing site is located, as well as the manufacturer and marketer of the concerned drug.
The proposed arrangement is aimed at ensuring timely communication of NSQ findings to the relevant authorities and stakeholders, thereby facilitating coordinated regulatory action and strengthening accountability across the drug manufacturing and marketing chain.
The proposed amendments follow deliberations at the 65th meeting of the Drugs Consultative Committee (DCC), held on 20 December 2024, and recommendations of the 92nd meeting of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB), held on 24 April 2025.
The amendments are expected to strengthen post-marketing regulatory surveillance, facilitate timely action against substandard medicines, promote greater accountability among manufacturers and marketers, and reinforce public confidence in the quality of medicines available in the country.
The initiative reflects the Government of India's continued commitment to strengthening the drug regulatory framework and ensuring the availability of safe, effective and quality medicines for the public.
The draft amendments have been notified for public consultation
, inviting objections and suggestions from stakeholders and members of the public within 30 days from the date on which copies of the Gazette of India containing the draft rules are made available to the public.
Objections and suggestions, if any, may be addressed to the Under Secretary (Drugs), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, U-6, Work Hall-C Wing, First Floor, Kartavya Bhawan-1, New Delhi – 110001, or sent by email to
drugsdiv-mohfw@gov.in
.
