title: Union Ministry of Health Proposes Amendments to Schedule M to Align Grade A Microbial Monitoring Requirements with WHO Guidelines
subtitle: The Proposed Amendment to Strengthen Microbial Monitoring in Grade A Areas and Align Sterile Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Standards with WHO Guidelines
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:

                04 NOV 2026 2:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to Schedule M of the Drugs Rules, 1945, vide G.S.R. No. 953(E) dated 28 October, 2026, to revise the prescribed limits for microbial contamination in Grade A clean areas in accordance with the World Health Organization (WHO) Technical Report Series (TRS) No. 1044, Annexure 2, on Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for Sterile Pharmaceutical Products.
The proposed amendment aims to address the existing differences between the microbial contamination limits prescribed under Schedule M and the corresponding WHO requirements for Grade A areas, thereby bringing India's regulatory provisions in line with internationally recognised standards.
Grade A areas are critical zones in sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing, where exposed products, containers and sterilised components are handled. Maintaining stringent microbial control in these areas is essential to ensuring the quality and safety of sterile pharmaceutical products.
The proposed revision will harmonise the Revised Schedule M with WHO guidelines and further strengthen the regulatory framework governing sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing in the country. It also provides for treating any microbial growth detected in Grade A areas as a trigger for investigation, in accordance with WHO guidance.
The proposed amendment reflects the Government's commitment to strengthening quality standards in pharmaceutical manufacturing, aligning domestic regulatory requirements with international benchmarks and ensuring the quality and safety of pharmaceutical products.
Stakeholders and members of the public are invited to submit their objections and suggestions, if any, on the proposed amendment to the Under Secretary (Drugs Regulation), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, U-6, Work Hall, C Wing, First Floor, Kartavya Bhawan-1, New Delhi–110001, or via email at

title: PIB Nagpur's VARTALAP on ‘Naxal Mukt Bharat’ Highlights Security, Development and Community Engagement in Gadchiroli
subtitle: Security Operations, Development Initiatives and Rehabilitation Key to Building a Naxal-Free India: Shri.Sandeep Patil Special Inspector General of Police, Nagpur Range
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 7:02PM by PIB Mumbai
content:
Nagpur/Gadchiroli
, 4 November 2026
The Press Information Bureau (PIB), Nagpur, in collaboration with Gadchiroli Police, organised a one-day VARTALAP Media Workshop on the theme “Naxal Mukt Bharat” at Eklavya Hall, Police Headquarters, Gadchiroli, on November 4, 2026. Several journalists from Gadchiroli district participated in the workshop, which brought together senior police officials, subject experts and media professionals to deliberate on the changing security and development landscape of the region and the country's efforts to combat Left Wing Extremism.
The programme commenced with the welcome of distinguished guests, followed by introductory remarks by Shri Saurabh Khekde, Media and Communication Officer, PIB Nagpur. He highlighted the importance of VARTALAP as a platform for interaction between the Government and the media and emphasised the role of regional journalists in disseminating accurate information about Government initiatives and developments in the region.
Addressing the gathering virtually, Shri Sandeep Patil, Special Inspector General of Police, Anti Naxal Opwrations ANO, Nagpur Range, spoke on the subject of Urban Maoism and its wider implications. He highlighted how Gadchiroli has transformed from a Maoist-affected region into a Naxal-free district through sustained efforts, determined security operations and several operations of national importance. He said that Gadchiroli's journey demonstrates how a coordinated approach involving security forces, effective policing and development initiatives can bring lasting change. He also highlighted how Gadchiroli is now leading by example in the national endeavour towards a Naxal Mukt Bharat.
He highlighted the challenges posed by organised Maoist networks to constitutional democracy and explained how the Maoist movement extends beyond armed activities in remote areas.
He discussed the broader dimensions of the Maoist challenge, including its organisational structures, ideological influence and networks operating beyond conflict-affected areas. He also underlined the importance of addressing the challenge through a comprehensive approach that combines security measures with development and public awareness.
Shri Patil emphasised that the response to Left Wing Extremism must go beyond security operations and include efforts to strengthen democratic institutions, improve infrastructure and ensure the effective delivery of Government welfare schemes. He further observed that the true revolution is one brought about through the Constitution of India, dedicating this thought to Bharat Ratna Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar.
Shri P. Y. Ramana, Policy Analyst, delivered a session on Maoist Economics, explaining the economic dimensions of Left Wing Extremism and its links with local resources and economic activities. The discussion highlighted the significance of mineral wealth, local economic structures and the financial networks associated with Maoist activities.
He also discussed the importance of understanding the economic aspects of the conflict while examining the impact of such activities on local communities and development. The session highlighted the need for informed and balanced media reporting on the economic dimensions of Left Wing Extremism.
Gadchiroli's journey in combating Left Wing Extremism
Providing an operational overview, Shri M. Ramesh, Superintendent of Police, Gadchiroli, spoke about the district's journey in combating Left Wing Extremism and the changing security scenario over the years.
He highlighted the progress made in containing Maoist activities through sustained security operations, improved intelligence gathering and coordinated action. He also referred to significant operational developments during recent years, including major operations against Maoist cadres and the increasing number of surrenders.
He noted the importance of the changing security situation in the district and the progress made through sustained efforts of security forces. The focus on preventing fresh recruitment into Maoist organisations and encouraging cadres to surrender and return to mainstream society was also highlighted.
The operational discussion covered the importance of counter-insurgency capabilities, inter-state coordination, strengthening of security infrastructure and improved intelligence and surveillance mechanisms. The role of specialised forces such as C-60 in countering Maoist activities was also discussed.
Shri Kartik Lokhande,Senior  journalist, spoke on the post-Maoism scenario and discussed the changing situation in regions affected by Left Wing Extremism. The session highlighted the importance of documenting the transition taking place in such areas and bringing development-related changes and ground realities to public attention.
Delivering the vote of thanks, Shri Yogesh Kumar, IPS, Deputy Inspector General of Police, Nagpur Range, drew upon his experience of more than a decade of witnessing Gadchiroli's transformation from a Maoist-affected region towards becoming a Naxal-free district. He said that the biggest achievement of this journey has been winning the trust of local people in the Government and the mainstream. He also acknowledged the dedication, valour and supreme sacrifices of several police personnel and commandos who played a crucial role in making Gadchiroli Naxal-free. He emphasised that sustaining public trust in the system would remain a key priority.
Shri Karthik Madhira, Additional SP (Operations), Gadchiroli, and Shri Gokul Raj G., Additional SP (Administration), Gadchiroli, along with other senior police officials, were prominently present at the programme.
The VARTALAP emphasised the responsibility of regional media in reporting on the changing social and economic conditions, the impact of security operations and the rehabilitation of affected communities. It also underlined the need for balanced, fact-based reporting that captures both the challenges and the progress being made in the region.
The VARTALAP workshop provided a platform for journalists to interact with senior police officials and subject experts on the security, economic and developmental dimensions of the Naxal Mukt Bharat initiative. It highlighted the importance of a comprehensive approach involving security, governance, infrastructure development, welfare delivery, rehabilitation and community participation in ensuring lasting peace. The programme also familiarised media representatives with the role of PIB in disseminating information on Government policies, programmes and achievements, while emphasising the importance of informed, accurate and responsible reporting. The workshop concluded with feedback and interaction with participating journalists.

title: Department of Justice Organises Workshop on “eFiling 3.0: From Process to Practice” for Government Ministries and Departments
subtitle:
Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Highlights Benefits of Technology for Citizens in Justice Delivery

An Initiative under the eCourts Mission Mode Project
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 7:36PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India, organised a Workshop on “eFiling 3.0: From Process to Practice” today at Hall No. 5, Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The workshop, an initiative under the eCourts Mission Mode Project, brought together officers and representatives of various Ministries and Departments of the Government of India, the Member (Systems) of the eCommittee of the Supreme Court of India and senior officers of the National Informatics Centre (NIC). It aimed to familiarise Government officials with the eFiling 3.0 platform and its practical use.
Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Law and Justice, was the Chief Guest. The programme commenced with the lighting of the lamp by the dignitaries, followed by the National Song and the National Anthem.
In his welcome address, the Secretary (Justice) thanked the Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice for gracing the occasion as the Chief Guest. He described eFiling as a key component of eCourts Phase III, enabling litigants to institute cases electronically from anywhere in the country. He observed that the Government, being one of the largest litigants and a major stakeholder in the judicial system, handles a substantial volume of litigation. He emphasised the importance of aligning Government’s litigation-related processes with the digital systems adopted by courts, so as to facilitate seamless filing, improve access to case-related information and streamline the management of court-related documentation. He noted that eFiling would address the limitations of physical filing by enabling Government officers to institute cases electronically, irrespective of geographical constraints.
The Secretary drew attention to the litigation-management facilities available to Government Departments. He stated that user credentials for eOffice can also be used for eCourts Single Sign-On (SSO), through which government officials can track their cases and that fees can be paid online through ePay from the office. A video on the eCourts Project was also screened.
The Secretary highlighted that despite the Government being the largest litigant, eFiling across Government Ministries/Departments is not uniform. This workshop was therefore planned, under the guidance and support of the Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice, to sensitise officials and facilitate the wider and regular use of eFiling.
Addressing the gathering, the Hon’ble Minister observed that the adoption of new technologies is often accompanied by initial hesitation. Illustrating this through the evolution from the post office to the telephone and subsequently to mobile phones, he emphasised the need for a change in mindset to embrace technological advancements. He further emphasised that eFiling is an integral part of this technological transformation and is here to stay.
The Hon’ble Minister stated that technological interventions should primarily serve the interests of citizens and make public services more accessible and efficient. Highlighting the transformative role of technology in the judicial system, he noted that the introduction of video conferencing in courts has significantly facilitated the expeditious disposal of cases, while saving considerable time and cost. He further emphasised that digital interventions have reduced the need for government officials, advocates and litigants to travel to courts, thereby improving accessibility and efficiency in the delivery of justice. He observed that wider adoption of technology-driven solutions could further help address the challenge of pendency and expedite case disposal. Addressing concerns about the impact of technology on existing work practices, the Hon’ble Minister clarified that artificial intelligence cannot replace human beings and emphasised that technology should be viewed as an enabling tool to reduce human effort, facilitate work and improve efficiency.
Acknowledging that challenges will arise, the Hon’ble Minister called for explaining the technology and creating awareness among stakeholders to achieve ease of living.
The Vote of Thanks was proposed by the Joint Secretary (eCourts), Department of Justice, who thanked the Hon’ble Minister, the Secretary (Justice), the eCommittee, NIC and the participating Ministries and Departments. The Joint Secretary urged participating Ministries and Departments to sensitise their concerned personnel and facilitate the wider and regular use of eFiling 3.0 in their litigation-related work.
The technical sessions, conducted by NIC with practical demonstrations, covered:
Functioning of eCourts: an overview of the applications and services under the eCourts Project;
eCourts Single Sign-On (SSO) and the eCourts Services Mobile App;
eFiling 3.0: features and functions, including the facilities available to Government Pleaders and Government Departments; and
an open discussion with participating officers.
The workshop reaffirmed the Department of Justice’s continued efforts under eCourts Phase III towards end-to-end digital and paperless courts and citizen-centric judicial eServices, including the universal adoption of eFiling across all courts.

title: Cabinet approves continuation of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs) for expeditious trial of cases of rape and POCSO (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences) Act for a further period of five years (FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31)
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 3:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister, has approved the continuation of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), including exclusive POCSO Courts, for a further period of five years i.e. from 01.04.2026 to 31.03.2031. The Scheme has a total financial outlay of Rs.3,788.04 crore (Central Share of Rs.2,353.15 crore and State/UT Share of Rs.1,434.89 crore). The Central Share will be funded from the Nirbhaya Fund.
The major features of the approved Scheme are as follows:
Continuation of the Scheme for five years i.e. from 01.04.2026 to 31.03.2031.
The Scheme has provision of operationalisation of 850 Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), including exclusive POCSO Courts, across various participating States/Union Territories.
Provision of dedicated Judicial Officer, Special Public Prosecutor and 6 support staff to facilitate expeditious disposal of pending cases relating to rape and offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012.
Provision of financial assistance to participating States/UTs for meeting the operational expenditure of FTSCs, in accordance with the CSS funding pattern.
Major impact:
The continuation of the Scheme is expected to have the following major impacts:
Providing Speedy Justice:
Ensuring faster trials and timely justice for victims of sexual offences.
Reducing Pending Cases:
Reducing the number of pending cases of Rape and POCSO Act cases.
Child-Friendly and Victim-Centric Environment:
The Scheme encourages establishment of Vulnerable Witness Deposition Centres (VWDCs) and child-friendly court spaces to facilitate victim testimonies without causing further distress.
Reduced inequality:
By prioritizing cases involving vulnerable groups (women and children), the scheme intends to reduce inequalities in access to justice.
Implementation strategy and targets:
The Scheme shall be implemented by the Department of Justice in coordination with the respective State Governments and UT Administrations. The key implementation strategies and targets are as follows:
Expansion of Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs):
Provision of expansion of FTSCs from the current 779 to 850 so that the coverage can extend in additional districts. This expansion shall be on the basis of case pendency data across all States and Union Territories.
Dedicated Legal Support:
Introduction of a specialized Special Public Prosecutor assigned exclusively to each FTSC to ensure speedy trials.
Optimized Court Staffing:
Allocation of one Judicial Officer and six support staff per FTSC to streamline administrative workload and facilitate expeditious disposal of old cases
.
Financial assistance:
Central assistance shall be provided to participating States/UTs in accordance with the approved funding pattern and prescribed guidelines.
Monitoring and evaluation:

title: Cabinet Approves Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing with an Outlay of Rs.2,814 Crore for Lithium and Nickel processing
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 3:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the ‘Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing’ with a financial outlay of Rs.2,814 crore over a period of five years.
Processing of critical minerals remains geographically concentrated in a few global locations. This exposes supply chains to geopolitical disruptions, price volatility, and potential supply restrictions, posing severe threats to supply chain resilience and economic security. This has implications for national security, economic sovereignty, and the timely achievement of decarbonisation targets.
At present, India remains substantially dependent on imports for refined intermediates and high-purity materials, owing to the nascent stage of domestic beneficiation and processing infrastructure for critical minerals, including Lithium, Nickel, Cobalt. Domestic processing capacity for critical minerals remains limited, with commercial-scale projects facing challenges relating to high capital requirements, limited availability of suitable technologies and constrained access to raw materials. Domestic processing capacity is therefore imperative for maximising value addition, achieving import substitution, and establishing resilient end-to-end value chains.
Against this backdrop, the “Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing” has been formulated to provide targeted capital expenditure support for the establishment and operationalisation of domestic processing facilities. The scheme aims to develop domestic processing capabilities in India to support value addition within the country, reduce import dependence, and develop value chain. The scheme targets processing of Lithium and Nickel ores/intermediary products into high purity compounds. Cobalt is also expected to be recovered as a by-product of nickel production. This will support critical sectors such as electric mobility, Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), electronics, defence, speciality steel etc.
The proposed scheme envisages a total financial outlay of Rs.2,814 crore. The scheme period is from FY 2026-27 to 2030-31. Under the scheme, capital subsidy of 30% of eligible investment will be provided for setting up four critical mineral processing plants, comprising two lithium processing plants (with a minimum capacity of 30 kt each) and two nickel processing plants (with a minimum capacity of 50 kt each). The maximum capital support will be capped at Rs.500 crore per lithium beneficiary and Rs.900 crore per nickel beneficiary, respectively.
The selection of beneficiaries shall be carried out through a two-stage process. In the first stage, applications shall be assessed for technical qualification, and only technically qualified applicants shall be eligible to participate in the second stage of financial bidding. For each mineral, two beneficiaries shall be selected based on the least-cost criterion, i.e., the lowest CAPEX support sought by the bidders under the Scheme. The incentives will be disbursed in three tranches linked to the achievement of specified milestones.
The Scheme is an important step towards advancing the objectives of Atmanirbhar Bharat by supporting the development of resilient domestic processing infrastructure and strengthening India’s capabilities across the critical mineral value chain.

subtitle:

Mandatory domestic content requirement for BESS to promote indigenous manufacturing and reduce import dependence
date:

                04 NOV 2026 3:38PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) Scheme for Development of Grid-Scale Energy Storage Systems, with a total financial support of Rs.14,500 crore for the period FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. The scheme aims to support the development of 92 GWh of, yet to be commissioned; energy storage capacity across the country. The scheme will support creation of new capacities equivalent to 170% of the present-day Grid Scale Energy Storage System capacity in the country and help meet the required Grid Scale ESS capacity of 411 GWh by 2031-32.
The scheme marks a significant step towards strengthening India's power sector infrastructure, facilitating large-scale integration of renewable energy and ensuring reliable, affordable and round-the-clock power supply. It will also provide an impetus to domestic manufacturing of battery energy storage systems, reduce import dependence and enhance the country's long-term energy security.
The scheme envisages the development of 60 GWh of Hydro Pumped Storage Plant (PSP) capacity, 30 GWh of Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity and 2 GWh of capacity through alternative energy storage technologies, with a total estimated investment of Rs.97,600 crore. The VGF support will help improve the financial viability of these projects and accelerate the deployment of large-scale energy storage infrastructure in the country.
Energy storage capacity will be allocated through a tariff-based competitive bidding process. Public and private sector electricity distribution companies will be eligible for VGF support for BESS and Hydro PSP projects, while projects based on alternative energy storage technologies will be implemented by public and private sector entities.
A key objective of the scheme is to strengthen India's domestic energy storage manufacturing ecosystem through demand-side financial support and reduce dependence on imported components. To promote indigenous manufacturing, BESS projects will be subject to a minimum Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) of 40%. The requirement will encourage domestic manufacturing, create opportunities for Indian industry and complement existing supply-side incentives for battery manufacturing.
The scheme represents an important intervention towards building a flexible, resilient and future-ready electricity system. By accelerating the deployment of grid-scale energy storage, it will facilitate greater utilisation of renewable energy, address the variability of renewable energy generation and reduce dependence on conventional generation for meeting balancing round-the clock power supply. The initiative will strengthen grid stability, improve renewable energy integration, encourage domestic manufacturing and enhance India's energy security, while advancing the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

NIRDPR addressed branding, product design and packaging, along with export marketing for SHG enterprises. NABARD focused on scaling SHG enterprises through finance. UNICEF introduced digital courses on using AI to start and manage small enterprises, alongside financial literacy, with examples from Computer Didi and Didi ki Dukan enterprises showing how these tools can support small businesses.
Ten structured buyer-seller meets at the Meet and Greet Pavilion connected women entrepreneurs with corporate procurement and retail channels. Delegations included Fabindia and My e-Haat of the HCL Foundation, creating opportunities for business relationships beyond the exhibition.
The Convergence Pavilion brought together 20 Central and State Government departments, including MSME, Textiles, Agriculture and Tribal Affairs, to facilitate access to formal credit, Udyam registration and statutory certifications. Digital facilitation desks enabled digital transactions with 100% UPI adoption and onboarding onto the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), Flipkart Samarth and Meesho, helping rural enterprises access additional markets.
The SARAS Shakti Food Court featured 50 stalls operated by more than 200 women entrepreneurs from over 30+ States and Union Territories. Daily cultural programmes from more than 10 participating states including Ladakh, Andhra Pradesh, Punjab, Goa, Odisha and Chhattisgarh among others added to the experience, bringing together craft, cuisine and performing traditions from across India.
A key initiative taken by the collaborating partner, Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty (SERP), Government of Andhra Pradesh, was the ‘Entrepreneurship Development and Acceleration Programme (EDAP)’, organized on the sidelines of the Mela with India SME Forum as the nodal agency. The programme followed an enterprise pathway covering expert learning, product readiness, digital onboarding, pitching, Udyam registration and buyer engagement. It recorded 3,489 attendances at expert sessions, 138 live product pitches, 288 entrepreneurs received photography and packaging support, 452 sellers received Meesho onboarding support, and 3,383 new WhatsApp Business accounts with product catalogues went live. A total of 15,231 Udyam registrations through the SWAYAM Helpdesk was also achieved.
The Mela also incorporated practical measures to reduce single-use plastic and encourage sustainable event practices. A total of 2 lakh cloth bags were made available across 600+ stalls while 2,000 reusable glass or clay bottles were supplied to participating artisans to reduce plastic bottle use. 800 eco-friendly bamboo/water-hyacinth dust bins were also provided across stalls.
Overall, the First National SARAS Mela brought market exposure, enterprise learning, institutional support and digital access together in one venue, supporting rural women entrepreneurs in building customer relationships and exploring opportunities beyond the event.

title: Novel silicon chip allowing terahertz waves to pass through barriers could enable future 6G networks
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 5:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A new silicon chip that allows terahertz waves to pass through an engineered barrier with little loss, while carrying data at 100 Gbit/s, points to compact terahertz circuits for future 6G communication technologies.
Future sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks are expected to use terahertz frequencies, which lie between microwaves and infrared light and offer wide bandwidth. Guiding these waves through compact circuits is challenging, as bends, junctions and abrupt changes in a waveguide can scatter or reflect part of the signal, weakening it as it travels.
By arranging triangular holes in a carefully designed pattern in a silicon slab, researchers can create a photonic crystal that guides terahertz waves along the boundary between two regions. Such boundary channels resist certain kinds of backscattering, but a practical circuit must also tolerate deliberately introduced obstacles and changes in geometry.
Researchers at the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), approached this challenge through topological photonics and demonstrated data transmission at up to 100 gigabits per second (Gbit/s) across an engineered barrier. A single barrier added only about 1–2% loss, and two barriers in sequence about 2–3%. In a conventional, non-topological waveguide, a comparable barrier markedly reduces transmission.
The team designed a silicon photonic crystal whose structure mimics the honeycomb lattice of graphene, and created a barrier by changing the sizes of the triangular holes over a short section of the waveguide.
Transmission remained close to its barrier-free level as long as the barrier strength stayed below a characteristic coupling strength of the crystal. Because the barrier is set by hole geometry, this offers a practical design rule for such devices.
The researchers tested the concept in three devices fabricated on high-resistivity silicon, a material compatible with established semiconductor manufacturing: one with two barriers in sequence, one with an omega-shaped route containing four sharp bends and a central barrier, and a power splitter with a barrier in one of its two branches.
Measurements across 310–360 GHz agreed closely with simulations. In the splitter, the two output signals were nearly identical, showing that the barrier had little effect on transmission.
Figure 1.
Artistic illustration of photonic Klein tunnelling in a silicon valley photonic crystal chip. A terahertz signal carrying high-speed data crosses the engineered barrier (blue) without significant loss, supporting 100 Gbit/s data transmission for 6G communication.
In high-speed data tests, the double-barrier and omega-shaped devices carried 48 and 60 Gbit/s, respectively. The splitter supported 100 Gbit/s using QAM-32 modulation, which encodes information in the signal’s amplitude and phase. At this rate, a 5-gigabyte high-definition film could in principle be transferred in under half a second.
Figure 2.
The research team in the Meta Optics Laboratory (MetoLab), JNCASR, with the fabricated silicon chip used to demonstrate photonic Klein tunnelling.
The study was led by Dr Abhishek Kumar, Assistant Professor at JNCASR, where he heads the Meta Optics Laboratory (MetoLab), with Samina Mulla and Sangram Kumar Sadhu of JNCASR as joint first authors. Collaborators included Asif Iqbal M and N. S. Vidhyadhiraja (JNCASR); Siddhartha Lal (IISER Kolkata); Anshuman Kumar (IIT Bombay); Zhonghua Gu and Prakash Pitchappa (Institute of Microelectronics, A*STAR, Singapore, and Pascal Szriftgiser and Guillaume Ducournau (University of Lille and CNRS, France).
“Showing that terahertz waves can cross a barrier created simply by changing the hole geometry, while carrying 100 gigabits per second, suggests that this effect can become a useful design tool for terahertz chips,” said Dr Abhishek Kumar.
The results could help researchers develop terahertz circuits that route and split signals on a single chip with low loss. The team next plans to tune the barriers electrically, thermally or mechanically, which could allow a device to redirect signals between paths on demand. The work has been published in the journal
Advanced Materials
.

title: Advanced protective coatings to improve machining of critical superalloys can help aerospace, energy & petrochemical sectors
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
An advanced surface-engineering approach developed by scientists can help improve the durability of cutting tools used for machining super alloys.
This could help aerospace, energy and petrochemical sectors, where nickel-based superalloys are indispensable for components operating under extreme conditions.
Machining of super alloys for use in aircraft engines, power plants and petrochemical systems is a major manufacturing challenge. Nickel-based superalloys such as Inconel 718 (IN718), IN625 and IN617 possess exceptional strength and hardness which make them difficult to cut or shape. Rapid work hardening, poor thermal conductivity and strong chemical interaction with cutting tools accelerate tool wear, reduce productivity and increase manufacturing costs.
Scientists from the International Advanced Research Centre for Powder Metallurgy and New Materials (ARCI), Hyderabad, an autonomous R&D Centre of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) have developed and evaluated two nanocomposite protective coatings—Titanium Aluminium Silicon Nitride (TiAlSiN) and Chromium Aluminium Silicon Nitride (CrAlSiN)—on widely used tungsten carbide cutting tools.
The coatings were deposited in-house using cathodic-arc physical vapour deposition and this helped evaluate the performance of tools for milling of IN718, IN625 and IN617. The study examined both tool life and the mechanisms governing coating performance.
The research revealed an important finding: there is no single coating that performs best for every superalloy. The effectiveness of a protective coating depends significantly on the chemistry of the material being machined and its interaction with the coating.
For IN718, the TiAlSiN-coated tool improved tool life by about 80% compared with an uncoated tool, while for IN625, the improvement was about 60%. For IN617, however, CrAlSiN proved remarkably superior, increasing tool life by more than 200%. The results demonstrate that one coating may be better suited to IN718 and IN625, while another can perform substantially better for IN617. The findings provide a scientific basis for selecting coatings according to the specific alloy being machined.
Fig 1:
Advanced nanocomposite coatings significantly improve the life of tungsten carbide cutting tools. The results show that the optimum coating depends on the specific nickel-based superalloy being machined.
The researchers also investigated how cutting tools failed. A major cause of damage was repeated adhesion of workpiece material to the tool surface. During machining, a layer of the superalloy can stick to the cutting edge and, when it subsequently breaks away, it pulls tiny fragments from the tool, progressively causing chipping. The coatings helped delay this damage and extend tool life. Chipping and progressive wear were identified as the major failure modes, with abrasion, adhesion and attrition contributing to the overall wear process.
Fig2:
A Scanning Electron Microscope image of a cutting-tool edge showing workpiece adhesion, abrasion, chipping and lateral cracks—key mechanisms responsible for tool failure during machining of nickel-based superalloys.
The researchers also examined the metal chips generated during machining. The chips exhibited characteristic shear bands and serrated or saw-tooth patterns, reflecting the intense thermo-mechanical conditions during cutting. The degree of chip segmentation was related to tool performance, providing further insight into the complex machining behaviour of these advanced alloys.
Longer-lasting cutting tools can reduce downtime, improve productivity and lower the cost of machining high-value engineering components.
More significantly, the study points towards a science-based, application-specific approach to protective coatings. Rather than seeking a universally superior coating, manufacturers can select or design coatings based on the composition and behaviour of the particular alloy being machined. This can contribute to more efficient, reliable and cost-effective manufacturing of components made from advanced materials.
The research carried out at ARCI's Centre for Engineered Coatings, has been published in the journal
Materials Today Communications.
The study demonstrates that the key to improving the machining of some of industry's most demanding materials lies not merely in developing a better coating, but in matching the right coating to the right material.

title: CSIR and DAKSHIN-RIS join hands to advance Science, Technology and Innovation for the Global South
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:

content:
With a shared vision of strengthening capacity building, research collaboration, technology partnerships for the advancement of countries of the Global South, the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) and DAKSHIN – Global South Centre of Excellence at the Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS) signed a Letter of Association (LoA) on 3 November 2026.
DAKSHIN envisions fostering knowledge sharing and mutual learning among countries of the Global South by promoting the development of sustainable, affordable and locally relevant solutions. Through the sharing of resources, technology transfer, exchange of experiences and collaborative strategies, DAKSHIN seeks to address common developmental challenges and accelerate progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). In this context, CSIR brings to the partnership its extensive scientific and technological knowledge base, along with a portfolio of ready-to-deploy, affordable and adaptable technologies with significant relevance to the developmental needs of the Global South. These technologies offer considerable potential for wider dissemination, industry-led implementation and facilitation of entrepreneurship across partner countries.
Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Rama Swami Bansal, Head, International S&T Affairs Directorate, CSIR, underscored the importance of international engagement among countries of the Global South and highlighted the potential for developing innovative models of collaborative partnerships to address shared developmental priorities.
Professor Sachin Kumar Sharma, Director General, RIS, observed that the association with CSIR would mark a significant milestone in translating scientific expertise and technological innovations into collaborative, impactful solutions for countries across the Global South. He particularly highlighted the potential for cooperation in key areas such as healthcare, infrastructure, agriculture, the blue economy and the digital economy.
The key objectives of the LoA include:
Fostering joint policy studies to identify innovative and context-specific solutions to developmental challenges.
Engaging relevant institutions and agencies to facilitate the scaling up of development interventions.
Promoting capacity building, human resource development and skill upgradation.
Documenting and sharing development experiences, best practices and success stories to strengthen collective self-reliance among countries of the Global South.
The association is expected to provide a meaningful platform for enhancing South-South cooperation, catalysing international partnerships and facilitating the transfer, adaptation and deployment of appropriate science and technology solutions. By leveraging CSIR’s scientific and technological expertise and DAKSHIN’s global engagement platform, the collaboration aims to support the development and dissemination of affordable, sustainable and locally relevant technology solutions and products, contributing to inclusive growth and sustainable development across the Global South.

title: Union Minister Dr Virendra Kumar Launches ‘Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan’ to Strengthen Intergenerational Bonding
subtitle:
Campaign to Promote Sustained Intergenerational Engagement Through the ‘5C’ Model of Connect, Converse, Co-create, Contribute and Continue

Union Minister Administers Vayo Samman Pledge; Handbook Released and Vayo SAATHI Volunteer Initiative Launched

Two MoUs Signed And Exchanged With Shri Ram Chandra Mission And Adhyatma Vigyan Satsang Kendra In Presence Of Hon’ble Minister, Senior Officials

“This Deepavali, Let No Elder Be Left Alone”-Dr Virendra Kumar
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 7:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar today launched the ‘Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan’, a National Intergenerational Bonding Campaign, under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), in the National Capital here this evening.
The initiative marks an important step towards strengthening intergenerational solidarity and promoting a society that recognises and values the experience, wisdom and contributions of senior citizens.
The Minister also released the Handbook on Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan and launched the Vayo SAATHI volunteer initiative to mobilise citizens in support of senior citizens.
On the occasion, two Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with Voluntary organizations namely Shri Ram Chandra Mission (SRCM) and Adhyatma Vigyan Satsang Kendra (AVSK), Jodhpur, were signed and formally exchanged in the presence of the Hon’ble Union Minister, Secretary MoSJE and other senior officials of the Ministry.
These collaborations aim to promote the holistic well-being of senior citizens through meditation, yoga and wellness programmes, besides encouraging intergenerational engagement through pledge drives, walkathons and other community-based activities.
Secretary, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, Additional Secretaries Smt Mona K Khandhar, Smt Debolina Thakur, Joint Secretaries Shri Sajeesh Kumar N, Dr Sandeep R Rathod, Shri Shailendra Kumar, Smt Monali P Dhakate, Shri Rahees M, Economic Advisor, Directors, Shri Astik Kumar Pandey, Ms Kajal Singh and other senior officials of the Ministry were present on the occasion.
Addressing the gathering, Dr. Virendra Kumar described the Abhiyan as an
‘Anubhav aur Urja ka Sangam’,
bringing together the experience of senior citizens and the energy of younger generations.
He highlighted that India's population aged 60 years and above is projected to increase from approximately 10 crore in 2011 to 23 crore by 2036.
The Minister observed that urbanisation, migration and changing family structures have reduced regular interaction between generations, resulting in challenges such as loneliness, limited awareness of welfare schemes and vulnerability to cyber fraud among senior citizens.
Emphasising the importance of mutual learning and intergenerational relationships, the Minister stated, “The youth will connect our elders to the digital world and our elders will give the youth the values of life.”
Giving a special message on the eve of Deepawali, he urged citizens to ensure that no elderly person in their homes or neighbourhoods is left alone and that one diya is lit in their honour.
The Minister highlighted that the Abhiyan would reach every village and mohalla through Panchayats, local bodies and educational institutions. He emphasised that even simple acts of care, such as spending half an hour with an elderly person or accompanying them to a doctor, represent meaningful contributions towards their well-being.
Dr Kumar said the Abhiyan reinforces the message that the welfare, dignity and inclusion of senior citizens are not merely governmental responsibilities but a shared social commitment.
During the programme, the Hon’ble Union Minister administered the Vayo Samman Pledge to all those present, encouraging collective commitment towards ensuring the dignity, care, respect and social inclusion of senior citizens.
Welcoming the gathering, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, stated that the initiative recognises senior citizens not merely as beneficiaries of welfare programmes but as active contributors, mentors and valuable repositories of knowledge, culture and social experience. He encouraged States and Districts to undertake activities in accordance with the Handbook to ensure effective implementation of the Abhiyan.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Abhiyan is based on the ‘5C’ model – Connect, Converse, Co-create, Contribute and Continue – which seeks to establish sustained engagement between generations.
He said Abhiyaan promotes connecting younger and older generations through community platforms and educational institutions, encouraging conversations and storytelling, undertaking joint activities, sharing knowledge and skills for community welfare, and continuing such engagement as a regular community-led practice rather than a one-time activity.
The Official said the Campaign encompasses twelve thematic areas, including
‘30 Minutes Together’, ‘Teach Me – I'll Teach You’, ‘My Story, My India’, ‘Digital Dada-Dadi / Digital Saathi’, ‘Generation Health & Wellness’ and ‘Silver Skills – Seniors as Mentors’
.
These themes aim to promote companionship, preserve oral histories, enhance digital literacy, create awareness about cyber fraud, encourage health and wellness, and recognise senior citizens as mentors and knowledge contributors, he said.
Another major component of the initiative is
Vayo SAATHI
(Support, Awareness, Assistance, Training, Health and Inclusion), a digitally enabled volunteer initiative open to all citizens aged 18 years and above, including students, young professionals and institutions, he said.
Volunteers will act as friends, facilitators and connectors for senior citizens, supporting their social inclusion and well-being adding that interested citizens can register through the SCW SAMAVESH Portal or JEEVAN App and receive a Vayo SAATHI Certificate, the Official further said.
The Official informed the Handbook released during the programme provides a comprehensive guiding framework covering the objectives, implementation strategy, thematic activities and roles of States, Districts and community institutions in carrying forward the Abhiyan.
The MoUs signed with Shri Ram Chandra Mission and Adhyatma Vigyan Satsang Kendra, Jodhpur, will further strengthen efforts towards the holistic well-being of senior citizens through meditation, yoga, wellness programmes and intergenerational engagement activities, he added.
Through Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan, the Ministry seeks to build a stronger culture of respect, care, companionship and solidarity across generations. The Department invites citizens, educational institutions, universities, youth organisations, NGOs, Resident Welfare Associations and CSR partners to participate in the initiative and register as Vayo SAATHI volunteers.

title: Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 Captivates Visitors with Vibrant Cultural Performances and Traditional Craftsmanship at Dilli Haat
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 6:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Shilp Samagam Mela 2026, currently underway at Dilli Haat, INA, New Delhi, continues to draw enthusiastic crowds with its spectacular display of India’s artistic traditions, indigenous craftsmanship, and vibrant cultural diversity.
Organised by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, the 15-day Mela has transformed into a bustling hub of inclusive celebration and will remain open to visitors until November 15, 2026.
Centred around the theme ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’, the Mela highlights India’s rich heritage of traditional crafts and festive lighting. The fair has been curated across seven distinct thematic zones to offer visitors a multi-sensory cultural experience.
These include कला आँगन featuring live craft demonstrations by skilled artisans, प्रकाश चौक displaying an exquisite collection of lamps and festive lights, पूजा पथ presenting a wide range of devotional products, सजावट बाज़ार focusing on unique and traditional home décor items, घराना featuring a stunning array of traditional textiles and fashion, स्वाद चौक offering diverse culinary delights from different regions, and मंच serving as the vibrant centre for cultural activities and evening performances.
The Mela features more than 130 stalls showcasing handicrafts, handloom products, and creative works by artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis, and persons with disabilities. To strengthen economic opportunities and market reach for these artisans, key empowerment components have been integrated into the event.
The Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022. Through 15 such fairs, more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.
This includes Bharat TULIP, which connects artisans directly with wider markets through e-commerce platforms, providing them with greater visibility, consumer access, and sustainable economic growth, alongside Purple Fest, which celebrates the creativity, capabilities, and active contributions of persons with disabilities while promoting equal opportunities and social inclusion.
A major attraction captivating visitors every evening is the series of cultural activities and programmes hosted at the
Manch
. Artists and troupe performers from different States come together to present colourful folk dances, traditional music, and regional art forms.
These evening programmes offer audiences a mesmerizing window into India's pluralistic cultural expressions on a single platform, creating a festive atmosphere and fostering regional cultural exchange.
Participating beneficiaries are supported by the Ministry's apex corporations, including the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), and National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC).
Artisans are provided with free stalls, travel expenses, daily allowances, and transportation facilities for their goods.
Through the Shilp Samagam Mela 2026, the Ministry continues its efforts to strengthen livelihood opportunities, encourage entrepreneurship, and foster inclusive economic growth while preserving India’s rich cultural heritage. The Ministry invites citizens, families, and art enthusiasts to visit Dilli Haat, explore traditional crafts, support artisan communities, and experience the nation's diverse cultural traditions.

title: A Rulebook Alone Cannot Guarantee Dignity; Every Hand in Aviation Must Ensure It: Manmeet Kaur Nanda
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 4:44PM by PIB Delhi
content:
“Merely framing rules, enforcing them or having a handbook will make no difference unless the last person dealing with a passenger with a disability understands and implements what is written in it.” Emphasizing the need to translate accessibility commitments into ground-level action, Ms. Manmeet Kaur Nanda, Additional Secretary, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), called for making continuous sensitization and training an integral part of India's aviation ecosystem to ensure safe, dignified and independent air travel for persons with disabilities.
Highlighting the human cost of inaccessible air travel, Ms. Nanda recounted the experience of a para-athlete who had to travel to Egypt and compete in an international sporting event using a broken wheelchair after her original wheelchair was damaged by an airline. Despite this ordeal, the athlete went on to win a medal. Describing such experiences as barriers that the entire aviation ecosystem must collectively eliminate, she stressed that airlines, airport operators, ground-handling personnel, security agencies, customs and immigration officials must undergo regular induction and refresher training. She underlined that the Handbook's coverage of all 21 specified disabilities, including invisible disabilities, would help build greater sensitivity and preparedness among frontline personnel. Calling for measurable accountability, she advocated accessibility performance indicators, time-bound grievance redressal mechanisms and dedicated dashboards to monitor the performance of airlines and airports. Reiterating the principle of “Nothing About Us Without Us”, she emphasized the active involvement of persons with disabilities as trainers and partners in shaping and evaluating aviation services.
Ms. Stuti Kacker, Former Secretary, DEPwD and Advisor, Asia-Pacific Network for Accessibility (APNA), highlighted the significant contribution of civil society organizations, disability rights activists, the media and the judiciary in advancing India's accessibility movement. Acknowledging the pioneering efforts of disability rights advocates, she observed that accessibility is a fundamental right, not an act of charity. She emphasized that Universal Design, inclusive mobility and sustained collaboration are essential to ensuring dignity, independence and equal opportunities.
Shri S. Govindraj, Commissioner, Office of the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities, highlighted the need to extend priority assistance to passengers with disabilities during deplaning, just as it is provided during boarding, to ensure a seamless and dignified travel experience. Mr. Prateek Sen of IndiGo emphasized that accessible physical infrastructure must be complemented by adequately trained personnel equipped with the right knowledge, attitude and soft skills. Reiterating the airline's philosophy of “Customers are the Core”, he stressed the importance of comprehensive sensitization and training across aviation services.
The “Sensitization and Training Handbook: Further Advancing the Accessibility of India’s Aviation Services” was officially launched on 4 November 2026 at the India International Centre, New Delhi. Developed by Samarthyam Centre for Universal Accessibility under the aegis of the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, in collaboration with the Ministry of Civil Aviation, the Handbook aims to strengthen institutional capacity and promote an inclusive, safe and passenger-friendly aviation ecosystem.
The Handbook provides practical guidance to airline personnel, airport operators, security staff and other aviation stakeholders on the rights and requirements of persons with 21 specified disabilities under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, relevant Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR), end-to-end passenger assistance, safety protocols, accessible communication and identification of barriers throughout the air travel journey. The launch was accompanied by a panel discussion featuring representatives from the Ministry of Civil Aviation, Airports Authority of India, Indian Aviation Academy, Office of the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities and IndiGo Airlines. Passengers with diverse disabilities also shared their lived experiences and perspectives, bringing the voice of the traveler to the center of the deliberations.
In her welcome address, Dr. Anjlee Agarwal, Founder Trustee, Samarthyam Centre for Universal Accessibility and Co-founder, Asia-Pacific Network for Accessibility (APNA), highlighted the pivotal role played by civil society in shaping India's journey towards accessibility and disability inclusion. She emphasized the importance of translating advocacy into institutional action through awareness, capacity building and sustained stakeholder engagement. Samarthyam, a not-for-profit organization working for the past 36 years to advance universal accessibility, inclusive mobility and disability rights through advocacy, capacity building and accessibility audits, has been instrumental in advancing this agenda. The initiative marks an important step towards transforming accessibility commitments into everyday practices, ensuring that every passenger can travel with confidence, dignity, independence and equal opportunity.

the support provided under the NAPDDR Scheme has marked an important step towards recovery, economic stability and a renewed sense of purpose.
His journey highlights the importance of timely intervention, sustained counselling, family participation and structured rehabilitation in helping individuals overcome substance dependence and rebuild their lives with dignity and confidence.
Mr Suresh Kumar, a resident of Karimnagar district in Telangana, faced significant personal, social and financial challenges due to prolonged alcohol and tobacco consumption. His journey towards substance dependence began during his late teenage years, largely influenced by peer pressure and emotional stress. Over time, his dependence intensified, adversely affecting his physical and mental health, family relationships and professional life.
The decline in his confidence, reduced motivation, irregular work attendance and financial instability further complicated his situation. His relationships with family members became strained, and he gradually withdrew from social interactions. Despite these difficulties, his family continued to support him and remained committed to helping him overcome his dependence.
A significant turning point came on 12 November 2025, when he received support at the Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA), operated by Prakriti Environment Society in Karimnagar, Telangana, under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
Through the intervention, he received comprehensive assistance, including individual counselling, group therapy, family counselling, motivational interviewing and relapse prevention therapy. Medical supervision and emotional support helped him address the challenges associated with substance dependence. Vocational guidance and rehabilitation services further supported his efforts to rebuild his confidence and reintegrate into family and social life.
With continued counselling, family involvement and structured rehabilitation, Mr. Kumar gradually regained control over his life. The intervention helped him develop healthier coping mechanisms, strengthen family relationships and work towards sustained recovery. The combined support of professional counselling and family participation played an important role in his progress towards a healthier lifestyle.
Today, Mr. Kumar is maintaining sobriety and leading a healthier and more stable life. He has resumed regular employment, actively participates in family and social activities, and has regained his confidence and motivation. His improved employment stability has also strengthened his financial position. From a phase of irregular earnings and financial difficulties, he is now earning approximately ₹15,000 per month.

Annual Survey of Industries: Volume-I publication contains detailed results of factory sector. This publication presents data relating to capital, employment, emoluments and several other economic parameters relevant to industrial sector such as (i) number of factories, (ii) fixed/working capital, (iii) total input, (iv) total output, (v) depreciation, (vi) gross value added, (vii) employment details, (viii) fuels consumption details, etc. The results are released at 2/3/4- digit industry-code wise [National Industrial Classification (NIC), 2008] for all-India and at 2/3-digit level of NIC-2008 for States/UTs.
In addition to Volume I, Summary Results for Factory Sector is prepared based on ASI 2024-25 results with the objective to draw attention to certain key features of the ASI results. The Summary Results for Factory Sector aims to present a comprehensive overview of the ASI findings through specialized tables highlighting key characteristics such as employment size, capital investment, gross output and net value added at both the national and State/UT levels. These tables provide an extensive summary of the industrial landscape at the regional as well as at the national level.

A brief note about the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) 2024-25
Coverage of ASI:
The Annual Survey of Industries broadly covers the following
Factories registered under Sections 2m(i) and 2m(ii) of the Factories Act,1948
Bidi and cigar manufacturing establishments registered under the Bidi & Cigar Workers (Conditions of Employment) Act,1966
Electricity undertakings engaged in generation, transmission and distribution of electricity, not registered with the Central Electricity Authority (CEA)
iv. Units with 100 or more employees registered in the Business Register of Establishments (BRE) prepared and maintained by the State Governments as and when such lists are shared by the respective State Governments.
ASI frame and its updation
The ASI frame is based on the lists of registered factory / units maintained by the Chief Inspector of Factories (CIF) in each State and those maintained by registration authorities in respect of Bidi and Cigar establishments and electricity undertakings. The frame is being revised and updated periodically by the Regional Offices of the Field Operations Division of NSO in consultation with the Chief Inspector of Factories in the State. At the time of revision, the names of the de-registered factories are removed from the ASI frame and those of the newly registered factories are added. For the units selected in the last survey year (in this case 2023-24), relevant fields like Status Code, Frame industry (NIC 4 digit), Employee (Total persons engaged), Address etc. of frame for a given year, say, ASI 2024-25 are auto-updated dynamically based on the information collected during the last survey year.
Unit of Enumeration
The primary unit of enumeration in the survey is a factory in the case of manufacturing industries, a workshop in the case of repair services, an undertaking or a licensee in the case of electricity, gas & water supply undertakings and an establishment in the case of bidi & cigar industries. The owner of two or more establishments located in the same State and pertaining to the same industry group and belonging to census scheme is, however, permitted to furnish a single consolidated return. Such consolidated returns are common feature in the case of bidi and cigar establishments, electricity and certain public sector undertakings.
Data Collection Mechanism
Data for ASI are collected from the selected factories under the Collection of Statistics Act 2008 as amended in 2017 and Rules framed there under in 2011. The entire survey is conducted through a dedicated web-portal without any paper schedule. For data collection in ASI, an establishment (and not enterprise) approach is followed wherein data are collected from the selected establishments.

title: Cabinet approves ‘Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR)’, a central sector scheme for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 NOV 2026 3:43PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today approved the ‘Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR)’ Scheme for the period FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31 with an outlay of Rs.4,371.10 crore.
Aligned with the central objective of Viksit Bharat 2047, the VISTAR Scheme is designed to establish a dynamic, real-time and future-ready official statistical architecture for enhanced timeliness, data granularity, interoperability with harmonised and AI ready datasets.
The VISTAR scheme will provide the strategic flexibility to dynamically allocate resources based on immediate policy needs, fostering a holistic approach to large-scale survey execution, methodological research, digital transformation, and national data governance. VISTAR Scheme will encompass all statistical and data management activities of MoSPI and it will play a crucial role for upgrading the official statistical system of the country. The three components of the VISTAR scheme are as follows:
Component 1: Comprehensive Statistical Operations and Strengthening of Ecosystem
Component 2: Support for Statistical Strengthening (SSS)
Component 3: Economic Census (EC)
Under the Comprehensive Statistical Operations and Strengthening of Ecosystem component, MoSPI proposes conducting 59 surveys during the 16th FC cycle, as compared to 43 major surveys conducted previously, potentially filling up critical data gaps in various sectors, thereby, improving decision-making and enabling timely and targeted policy interventions. In addition, building on recent digital transformations in technology enabled data collection and user-centric dissemination, MoSPI will focus on the end-to-end digitalization of statistical processes and embedding Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning into regular workflows, primarily for data processing, validation, and analysis.
MoSPI is planning to release new metrices, including the Headline Index of Services Production, the Index of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises. MoSPI will build upon the foundational pillars of data harmonisation such as data cataloguing, machine readability, interoperability, sharing protocols, and privacy by design etc. to dismantle silos and improve programme targeting, reduce duplication, and pave the way for AI-driven decision-making across government levels. By mainstreaming alternate sources—like mobile phone, scanner, and e-commerce data—MoSPI will aim to complement traditional surveys, reduce respondent burden, fill data gaps, and strengthen evidence-based policymaking. Furthermore, MoSPI will ensure capacity building and enhanced opportunities for youth and researchers through Internship Scheme for students and research proposals from academic & research institutions.
Under the Support for Statistical Strengthening (SSS) component, funds are to be provided to State/UT Governments for transforming the statistical capabilities of States and Union Territories through a redesigned, deliverable-linked framework (SSS 2.0). The vision focuses on building state-level capacity to generate high-quality, granular data at the district and other disaggregated levels, developing indigenous data processing capabilities, and embedding data use cases into localized policymaking. MoSPI will provide technical support to scale up generation of district-level estimates and million-plus city level estimates in flagship national surveys (e.g., PLFS, HCES, ASUSE) as well as in compilation of State/District level GDP and State level IIP.
Under the Economic Census (EC) component, MoSPI will undertake the 8th Economic Census (EC) in collaboration with the States / UTs which will provide granular data and activity details of all the non – farm establishments and workers hired, therein, upto Gram Panchayat and Ward level, providing an assessment of the unorganized sector of the economy and will serve as the baseline for developing National Statistical Business Register (SBR) to facilitate targeted enterprise surveys and strategic interventions. The economic census data will be extremely useful for planners and policy makers at national and sub-national levels, which will pave way for estimating the contribution of unorganized sector to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
